topics.text:
jaato-scaffold — interrogate the installed framework, then build.

  24 providers   48 plugins   4 gc strategies   10 archetypes

drill down:
  jaato-scaffold explain plugins
  jaato-scaffold explain plugin <name>
  jaato-scaffold explain commands
  jaato-scaffold explain providers
  jaato-scaffold explain provider <name>
  jaato-scaffold explain gc
  jaato-scaffold explain env [<filter>]                           # vars the daemon + plugins READ
  jaato-scaffold explain events [<filter>]                        # the client/server protocol
  jaato-scaffold explain event <NAME or wire.value>               # one event's fields + docstring
  jaato-scaffold explain transports
  jaato-scaffold explain clients
  jaato-scaffold explain runtime
  jaato-scaffold explain tiers
  jaato-scaffold explain integrations                             # tools jaato can wire into
  jaato-scaffold explain releases                                 # newer builds on PyPI / TestPyPI
  jaato-scaffold explain sets [--workspace DIR]
  jaato-scaffold explain agents [--workspace DIR]                 # the PERSONA layer (.jaato/agents/)
  jaato-scaffold explain services [--workspace DIR]               # named HTTP APIs (.jaato/services/)
  jaato-scaffold explain profile [<name>] [--workspace DIR]       # a session's CAPABILITIES
  jaato-scaffold explain oversight [<profile>] [--workspace DIR]  # the HUMAN-OVERSIGHT measures (EU AI Act Art. 14)
  jaato-scaffold explain audit [<profile>] [--workspace DIR]      # the AUDIT RECORD (EU AI Act Arts. 12, 19)
  jaato-scaffold explain paths
  jaato-scaffold explain gh                                       # driving `gh` / `git` with a per-user token
  jaato-scaffold explain runner-user                              # which OS account a root daemon's runners run as
  jaato-scaffold explain pool                                     # the pre-warm runner pool, resized live
  jaato-scaffold explain prefetch
  jaato-scaffold explain completion                               # the OUTPUT-side hook
  jaato-scaffold explain archetypes                               # what `new` WRITES
  jaato-scaffold explain archetype <name>

`dependencies` (or `deps`) is a FACET, not a topic: it is accepted in
any position after `explain` and consumed before the topic is looked
up, so it never appears in the list above.  It is also not a facet of
every topic — only a NAMED provider or plugin has one of its own;
anything else, a bare `explain dependencies` included, answers with the
framework picture and says so.  Derived by parsing what is installed,
never from a table that could be wrong:
  jaato-scaffold explain dependencies           # distributions, skew, extras
  jaato-scaffold explain provider <name> deps   # what its code imports
  jaato-scaffold explain plugin <name> deps
a named unit is read as its own source PLUS the shared machinery it
imports, and a MISSING package is printed with the extra declaring it.

integrations ship WITH this build, so an installed copy cannot describe a
different framework than the one running:
  jaato-scaffold integration               # list them + their state
  jaato-scaffold integration claude-code   # -> ~/.claude/skills/ (all repos)
  jaato-doctor                             # says when one has gone stale

flags.effect: IPCClient over a Unix socket + SOCKET constant; auto_start=True so the script cold-starts a daemon
WSClient + URL/TOKEN (and CA) constants; --ca is threaded as the scoped ca= knob, never os.environ
InProcessClient — imports from `jaato`, no socket/url constants, runs the runtime in the script's own process; rejects --recoverable
upgrades a daemon transport to its auto-reconnect client (IPCRecoveryClient / WSRecoveryClient) and adds an on_status_change callback that prints the connection lifecycle

REQUIRED for the archetypes that CREATE a session from an inline spec (client / fire / host-tools), and for --transport in_process on ANY archetype (the embedded client IS the binding).  OPTIONAL for cascade / sweep / observer: omit both and the stage/job placeholder is a profile NAME instead of an inline spec, no MODEL/PROVIDER constants are emitted, and .env gets no provider stanza.  Supplying one without the other is refused — half a binding reads as a working spec and is not
overwrite an existing run_<archetype>.py / .env
no effect on the emitted files — only on the credential hint printed afterwards (they shape a profile-set's YAML, not a client)

generated_correct: the turn goes through the SDK's convenience facade (<Client>.session(...) -> Session.ask / .stream / .complete), not a hand-rolled asyncio.Event + subscribe + done.wait() loop.  That recipe is what convenience.py exists to own, it is subtle enough that the canonical template once shipped an infinite hang (PR #399), and a hand-rolled copy silently misses whatever the facade learns next — as it already had, with the settle rule of #767 (jaato #825/#826/#827)
client_type=ClientType.API — load-bearing: the daemon keeps signal_completion for API clients and strips it for TERMINAL/WEB/CHAT
connect_timeout=120.0 — a cold daemon autostart takes ~30-60s; the SDK default of 5s is too short

session_timeout=60.0 beside it — the session.new confirmation budget, a different clock from connect_timeout; raise it when several sessions open close together on one daemon (one measured 19.4s under cascade load), because on expiry a session MAY exist and a retry makes a second one
env_file is always a real path — env_file=None crashes the IPC handshake with an opaque os.PathLike TypeError

WHICH turn method: ask/stream for a NON-GATED session (its turn IS the terminus; the turn event PROPOSES one, that agent's next status event CONFIRMS it, and SESSION_TERMINATED settles unconditionally — one rule parameterised by span since #1007, not first-of a pair), complete() for a COMPLETION-GATED one (an agent that ends a turn without signal_completion is re-prompted and keeps working, so the turn event fires mid-flight — jaato #767).  complete() also RETURNS the typed AGENT_COMPLETED payload; waiting on the terminal event alone tells you that a session ended and nothing about what it produced
create_session RAISES SessionCreateFailed; it does not return None, and the facade lets it out of the context manager rather than yielding a dead session
an error terminal arrives as a typed AgentError (error_type + error_summary), not as a reason string to compare against
data.name: cascade

detail: a linear CHAIN: a WORKLIST of (profile, agent, prompt) stages run one at a time, each to terminal completion before the next starts

each stage is `await stage.complete(prompt)` and RETURNS the stage's typed payload — a driver that waits on the terminal event alone learns that a stage ended and nothing about what it produced (jaato #827)
one cascade id (uuid) tenants every stage, so an observer can attach to the whole run and the stages share one warm slot
for INDEPENDENT jobs that do not feed forward, use `sweep` instead
writes.what: the runnable SDK client — a complete, executable Python script

detail: JAATO_PROVIDER=<provider> and MODEL_NAME=<model> — active, from the flags.  Absent entirely when no binding was supplied (cascade / sweep / observer without --provider/--model): the profile each stage names owns them, and a provider nobody chose would read as guidance rather than the throwaway it is
the chosen provider's env vars, commented out (all of them — they are your provider config); no provider stanza at all when none is bound
every OTHER framework knob that has a meaningful default, commented out and grouped by category — discovered from the installed code, so it cannot drift from what the daemon reads
the provider credential is NOT written — set it yourself (`jaato-scaffold explain provider <name>` names the variable)
writes.what: workspace env: the active provider/model plus every optional knob, commented out with its default

generated and correct — the recipe this archetype exists to carry:
  - the turn goes through the SDK's convenience facade (<Client>.session(...)
    -> Session.ask / .stream / .complete), not a hand-rolled asyncio.Event +
    subscribe + done.wait() loop.  That recipe is what convenience.py exists
    to own, it is subtle enough that the canonical template once shipped an
    infinite hang (PR #399), and a hand-rolled copy silently misses whatever
    the facade learns next — as it already had, with the settle rule of #767
    (jaato #825/#826/#827)
  - client_type=ClientType.API — load-bearing: the daemon keeps
    signal_completion for API clients and strips it for TERMINAL/WEB/CHAT
  - connect_timeout=120.0 — a cold daemon autostart takes ~30-60s; the SDK
    default of 5s is too short
  - session_timeout=60.0 beside it — the session.new confirmation budget, a
    different clock from connect_timeout; raise it when several sessions open
    close together on one daemon (one measured 19.4s under cascade load),
    because on expiry a session MAY exist and a retry makes a second one
  - env_file is always a real path — env_file=None crashes the IPC handshake
    with an opaque os.PathLike TypeError
  - WHICH turn method: ask/stream for a NON-GATED session (its turn IS the
    terminus; the turn event PROPOSES one, that agent's next status event
    CONFIRMS it, and SESSION_TERMINATED settles unconditionally — one rule
    parameterised by span since #1007, not first-of a pair), complete() for a
    COMPLETION-GATED one (an agent that ends a turn without signal_completion
    is re-prompted and keeps working, so the turn event fires mid-flight —
    jaato #767).  complete() also RETURNS the typed AGENT_COMPLETED payload;
    waiting on the terminal event alone tells you that a session ended and
    nothing about what it produced
  - create_session RAISES SessionCreateFailed; it does not return None, and
    the facade lets it out of the context manager rather than yielding a dead
    session
  - an error terminal arrives as a typed AgentError (error_type +
    error_summary), not as a reason string to compare against

  --transport ws --url URL [--token T] [--ca BUNDLE]
        WSClient + URL/TOKEN (and CA) constants; --ca is threaded as the
        scoped ca= knob, never os.environ
  --transport in_process
        InProcessClient — imports from `jaato`, no socket/url constants, runs
        the runtime in the script's own process; rejects --recoverable
  --recoverable
        upgrades a daemon transport to its auto-reconnect client

        REQUIRED for the archetypes that CREATE a session from an inline spec

        / sweep / observer: omit both and the stage/job placeholder is a

        are emitted, and .env gets no provider stanza.  Supplying one without
        the other is refused — half a binding reads as a working spec and is
        not
  --force
        overwrite an existing run_<archetype>.py / .env
  --secrets / --secret-path
        no effect on the emitted files — only on the credential hint printed
        afterwards (they shape a profile-set's YAML, not a client)

jaato-scaffold new dossier

  component pack for jaato itself (--component).

required: --workspace --profile or --component

      the Annex IV technical documentation for the system that profile defines
      — computed sections filled, the rest marked TODO in the Article's own
      words

        fill says so rather than being omitted, because an absent section in a
        legal document reads as *nothing to declare*
      - every computed fact comes from the helper the matching `explain` page
        reads, so the dossier cannot disagree with `explain`
      - each computed section is dated and stamped with the commit it
        describes — a fact about a tree is a fact about a commit

        harness's own caveats verbatim

      the Article 25(4) information pack for jaato as a component of somebody
      else's high-risk system
      - what the framework GUARANTEES, each named with the thing that enforces
        it — a guarantee with no enforcer is a claim, and a claim in a 25(4)
        pack is what gets relied on
      - what it does NOT guarantee, said out loud
      - the versioned surfaces a written agreement can cite

  --transport ipc (default)
        IPCClient over a Unix socket + SOCKET constant; auto_start=True so the
        script cold-starts a daemon

archetypes.text:
`jaato-scaffold new <archetype>` — what each one WRITES into your
workspace.  Every archetype re-checks its own output — see each
one's `check` under `explain archetype <name>`.

  profile-set   [default, also `set`]
      Two-tier profile set — a provider-agnostic base per stage plus a
      provider/model binding for each.
      writes: .jaato/profiles/_base_<agent>.yaml,
              .jaato/profiles/<set>/<agent>.yaml, .env, .gitignore,
              .jaato/scaffold.json
      needs:  --workspace --set --provider --model --agents

  cascade
      Cascade driver — sequential multi-session stages.
      writes: run_cascade.py, .env
      needs:  --workspace

  client
      Minimal jaato SDK client — single session, send + wait.
      writes: run_client.py, .env
      needs:  --workspace --provider --model

  dossier
      The EU AI Act paperwork this tree can compute: an Annex IV technical-
      documentation skeleton for one profile (--profile), or the Article
      25(4) component pack for jaato itself (--component).
      writes: docs/annex-iv-<name>.md, docs/jaato-component-pack.md
      needs:  --workspace --profile or --component

  fire
      Fire-and-forget jaato SDK client — send, do not wait.
      writes: run_fire.py, .env
      needs:  --workspace --provider --model

  gitignore
      The workspace .gitignore block that keeps .jaato/ runtime state
      (sessions, logs, memories, stored credentials) out of git and its
      authored assets (profiles, agents, schemas, processors) in — the fix
      `validate`'s gitignore_* findings name.
      writes: .gitignore
      needs:  --workspace

  host-tools
      Client-provided ('host') tools — the agent calls a tool YOUR client
      runs.
      writes: run_host-tools.py, .env
      needs:  --workspace --provider --model

  observer
      Cascade observer — attach + live-trace events (read-only).
      writes: run_observer.py, .env
      needs:  --workspace

  processor
      A completion processor — kb Python that gates signal_completion, with
      the bounded-refusal contract already right.
      writes: .jaato/scripts/processors/<name>.py, .gitignore
      needs:  --workspace --name

  sweep
      Sweep/matrix driver — N INDEPENDENT jobs, none feeding another.
      writes: run_sweep.py, .env, acceptance.sh,
              .jaato/scripts/processors/<name>.py,
              .jaato/completion_schemas/<name>.json,
              .jaato/profiles/<name>.yaml, .gitignore
      needs:  --workspace

fields.description: which kind of record this is
fields.name: stage

fields.description: NEW, uncached input tokens -- excludes both cache counts (#758)
fields.name: prompt_tokens

fields.description: the authenticated user the session runs as (#859)
fields.name: user_id

events.note: A provider that reported NO usage writes the three token fields as null rather than omitting them, because a reported zero and an unreported one are different facts (#688) and `TokenUsage.reported` is what tells them apart

events.article: Art. 50(1) -- the person was told, and what they were told

fields.description: which kind of record this is
fields.name: stage

fields.description: the session the person was talking to
fields.name: session_id

fields.description: `main` -- the agent that fronts the person; a subagent talks to its parent and is never announced
fields.name: agent_id

fields.description: True iff the text reached a client. The one question an auditor asks, answered by construction: a row carries `text` exactly when this is True and `withheld_reason` exactly when it is False
fields.name: delivered

fields.description: True when the CLIENT asserted it discloses already (client_discloses_ai) and the framework withheld its own text: the record then says the client took the obligation -- suppressed, never absent
fields.name: suppressed

fields.description: True on a session woken from disk: nothing is re-announced, because the person was told before the transcript they are looking at began, and the row says so rather than leaving the wake unrecorded
fields.name: revived

fields.description: the announcement as delivered, verbatim -- a hash would not answer WHAT was said. Present only when `delivered` is True
fields.name: text

fields.description: why nothing was delivered, when nothing was: `client_discloses` (the client took the obligation), `headless` (the session was created for no client, so the event reached nobody), `decision_failed` (the predicate raised, so whether an announcement was owed could not be established), `wake` or `reattach` (a revive -- a deliberate session.wake, or a client attaching to a session the daemon had unloaded; a long-lived interactive session accumulates many of the second)
fields.name: withheld_reason

fields.description: the channel: PresentationContext.client_type (terminal / web / chat / api). Absent on a revive, where no client is attached yet
fields.name: client_type

fields.description: the client's own assertion, as received; absent when no client had declared a presentation
fields.name: client_discloses_ai

audit.text:
the audit record  (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Arts. 12, 13(3)(f), 19)
  schema version 2

  NOT a sixth store -- a CONTRACT over the stores that already record.
  13(3)(f) asks the instructions for use to describe the mechanisms a
  deployer collects, stores and interprets the logs with; this page is
  that description, computed rather than written down beside the code.

STORES
  ledger
      where:  trace.ledger  (env: LEDGER_PATH)
      format: JSONL, one object per record, appended as it is recorded
        Every model round trip and every permission verdict. Appended per
        record since #1109, so a process that dies mid-turn has written what
        it recorded
        governed by retention_days
  session_trace
      where:  trace.session_log  (env: JAATO_TRACE_LOG)
      format: line-oriented; the DECISION lines are `key=value`, reason last
        The application trace: permission DECISION lines (#951/#968), budget
        ceilings and rungs (#955), tool-runner resolve/result lines. The one
        artefact every deployment gets
        governed by retention_days
  provider_trace
      where:  trace.provider_log  (env: JAATO_PROVIDER_TRACE)
      format: JSONL, one object per provider interaction
        What went to the model and what came back, per agent. The largest
        store by far and the one a retention policy usually shortens first
        governed by retention_days
  session_record
      where:  <workspace>/.jaato/sessions/<session_id>/
      format: JSON
        The session's own state: history, profile snapshot, creator, runner
        identity. This is the CONVERSATION, not the audit log --
        `conversation_retention_days` governs it, and it may be deleted while
        the audit record is kept
        governed by conversation_retention_days -- this is the CONVERSATION,
        not the log about it

EVENTS
  response   -> ledger
      Art. 12(1) -- each model round trip
      written by jaato_server/shared/jaato_session.py::_record_token_usage
        stage              which kind of record this is
        ts                 unix timestamp
        iso_ts             the same instant, ISO-8601 UTC
        event_index        position in this ledger
        prompt_tokens      NEW, uncached input tokens -- excludes both cache counts (#758)
        output_tokens      tokens the model produced
        total_tokens       as the provider reported it
      ? user_id            the authenticated user the session runs as (#859)
      ! A provider that reported NO usage writes the three token fields as
        null rather than omitting them, because a reported zero and an
        unreported one are different facts (#688) and `TokenUsage.reported` is
        what tells them apart
  announcement   -> ledger
      Art. 50(1) -- the person was told, and what they were told
      written by jaato_server/shared/ai_disclosure.py::announcement_record
        stage              which kind of record this is
        ts                 unix timestamp
        iso_ts             the same instant, ISO-8601 UTC
        event_index        position in this ledger
        session_id         the session the person was talking to
        agent_id           `main` -- the agent that fronts the person; a subagent talks to its parent and is never announced
        delivered          True iff the text reached a client. The one question an auditor asks, answered by construction: a row carries `text` exactly when this is True and `withheld_reason` exactly when it is False
        suppressed         True when the CLIENT asserted it discloses already (client_discloses_ai) and the framework withheld its own text: the record then says the client took the obligation -- suppressed, never absent
        revived            True on a session woken from disk: nothing is re-announced, because the person was told before the transcript they are looking at began, and the row says so rather than leaving the wake unrecorded
      ? text               the announcement as delivered, verbatim -- a hash would not answer WHAT was said. Present only when `delivered` is True
      ? withheld_reason    why nothing was delivered, when nothing was: `client_discloses` (the client took the obligation), `headless` (the session was created for no client, so the event reached nobody), `decision_failed` (the predicate raised, so whether an announcement was owed could not be established), `wake` or `reattach` (a revive -- a deliberate session.wake, or a client attaching to a session the daemon had unloaded; a long-lived interactive session accumulates many of the second)
      ? client_type        the channel: PresentationContext.client_type (terminal / web / chat / api). Absent on a revive, where no client is attached yet
      ? client_discloses_ai the client's own assertion, as received; absent when no client had declared a presentation
      ? locale             the BCP 47 tag the client declared for the person's interface; absent when it declared none -- never defaulted from the daemon's own environment
      ? provider           the binding active at the announcement -- the same pair `generated_by` stamps on the model's own output
      ? model              its other half
      ? created_by         the authenticated creator (#859)
      ! Written by the DAEMON at session creation, before the first turn, into
        the same file the runner's ledger then appends to: the chain belongs
        to the FILE, so the two writers continue one chain and the
        announcement precedes the first `response`. `event_index` is per
        writer, so on a runner-served session the announcement and the first
        response can both carry 0 -- the chain, not the index, is the order.
        Written only for a profile declaring interacts_with_persons: true; a
        profile that made no determination gets no row, because a row would be
        one. With no ledger file configured (trace.ledger / LEDGER_PATH) the
        row is held in memory and never reaches disk -- announced at WARNING,
        and `validate` reports the profile as disclosure_unrecorded (#1157)
  permission-check   -> ledger
      Art. 12(1), 14(4)(d) -- each tool call's verdict
      written by jaato_server/shared/ai_tool_runner.py::_permission_gate_verdict
        stage              which kind of record this is
        ts                 unix timestamp
        iso_ts             the same instant, ISO-8601 UTC
        event_index        position in this ledger
        tool               the tool asked for
        args               the arguments it was asked with
        allowed            the verdict
        reason             the verdict in words
        method             HOW it was reached: whitelist / default / allow_all / a channel answer / an evaluator
      ? agent              which session asked (#951)
      ? call_id            correlates to the tool call
      ? user_id            who answered, when anybody did (#859)
      ? approver           the name an external approval system attached (#859); asserted, recorded as claimed
      ! `user_id` and `approver` are ABSENT for a policy decision. That is the
        point: 'nobody was asked' must stay distinguishable from 'somebody
        answered'
  DECISION   -> session_trace
      Art. 12(1), 14(4)(d) -- the same verdict, in the one artefact every deployment gets
      written by jaato_server/shared/plugins/permission/plugin.py::check_permission
        tool               the tool asked for
        call_id            correlates to the tool call
        agent              which session asked
        session            the daemon session id
        allowed            the verdict
        method             how it was reached
        asked              whether a HUMAN was consulted -- the fact `method` could not supply, since allow_all and the two suspensions are each produced both by a pre-approval and by somebody typing a key (#968)
        policy             runtime or session-scoped (#957)
      ? user_id            who answered
      ? approver           an external approver's claim
        reason             free text, LAST, so the line parses
      ! Machine-readable by construction: scalars first, free-text `reason`
        last. `parse_decision_trace` reads it back. The ledger's row needs a
        ledger and the event is opt-in; this line is what a deployment has
        without configuring anything
  BUDGET CEILING / BUDGET RUNG   -> session_trace
      Art. 12(1), 14(3)(a) -- a built-in constraint acting
      written by jaato_server/shared/jaato_session.py::_apply_budget_rungs
        dim                which dimension crossed
        used               what had been spent
        limit              the declared ceiling
      ? at                 the rung's percentage
      ? action             what the rung did
      ! A ceiling is traced whether or not a rung fires: a ladder that never
        logs is indistinguishable from one that is not wired (#955)
  INCIDENT   -> session_trace
      Arts. 72, 73, 26(5) -- something a person should look at
      written by jaato_server/shared/incidents.py::raise_incident
        kind               which of the framework's known incident kinds (shared.incidents.INCIDENT_KINDS)
        at                 when the framework became AWARE -- Art. 73's three reporting clocks all start here
        cause              one line, LAST, so the line parses
      ? site               file.py::function -- what noticed
      ? session_id         the session it happened in
      ? provider           the binding that was serving
      ? model              the model that was serving
      ? tier               the tier, on a tiered session
      ! Carries NO severity, and the absence is the decision rather than an
        omission: whether an entry is a 'serious incident' under Art. 3(49) is
        a determination about consequences -- harm to a person, disruption of
        critical infrastructure -- that no log line carries. `jaato-doctor
        --incidents` renders all three Art. 73 windows beside each row and
        chooses none
  session record header   -> session_record
      Art. 12(1) -- the session's own lifecycle
      written by jaato_server/server/session_manager.py::_save_session
        session_id         the id
        version            record version
      ? created_by         the authenticated creator (#859, record 2.9+)
      ? runner_identity    which runner ran it (#812, record 2.10+); `stale` after a reload, because the pid named is from a previous process lifetime
        profile_snapshot   the resolved recipe the session froze (#787)
        sandbox_mode       apparmor / apparmor-complain / soft (#1014) -- whether a boundary was ENFORCED, not merely provisioned

  '?' marks a field present only when it was MEASURED.  Absent is not
  zero and is never written as null -- a provider that reported no
  cache must not read as a cache that never hit.

  `explain audit <profile> --workspace DIR` shows the concrete paths
  THAT profile writes to and what its record_keeping: block says.

data.turn_method_rule: WHICH turn method: ask/stream for a NON-GATED session (its turn IS the terminus; the turn event PROPOSES one, that agent's next status event CONFIRMS it, and SESSION_TERMINATED settles unconditionally — one rule parameterised by span since #1007, not first-of a pair), complete() for a COMPLETION-GATED one (an agent that ends a turn without signal_completion is re-prompted and keeps working, so the turn event fires mid-flight — jaato #767).  complete() also RETURNS the typed AGENT_COMPLETED payload; waiting on the terminal event alone tells you that a session ended and nothing about what it produced

turn_methods.name: ask
turn_methods.on_session_end: raises SessionEnded unless the reason is clean
turn_methods.use_for: a conversation — the session survives, ask again

turn_methods.name: stream
turn_methods.on_session_end: yields what it had, then raises SessionEnded
turn_methods.use_for: the same turn, rendered as it arrives

turn_methods.name: complete
turn_methods.on_session_end: returns the payload; the ending is on Session.terminus
turn_methods.use_for: a cascade stage that produces one typed artifact and stops

clients.text:
Python SDK clients — one facade, one client per transport
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  InProcessClient     IPCClient          WSClient         IPCRecoveryClient
  - embedded          - local daemon     - remote daemon  - local daemon
    (no daemon)         (Unix socket)      (ws:// / wss://)  + auto-reconnect
  - lowest latency    - no reconnect     - bearer token   - on_status_change
  - simplest deploy   - one-shot/script  - jaato-sdk[ws]    survives restarts

  All expose the same Session.ask/.complete/.stream facade; pick the
  transport with jaato.session(mode='in_process'|'ipc'|'ws') and add
  recovery=True on a daemon mode for auto-reconnect.  Use --recoverable
  for anything long-lived (IPCRecoveryClient on ipc, WSRecoveryClient on
  ws) — it rides through a per-run `jaato-server --stop` + autostart; on a
  permanent IncompatibleServerError it stops rather than looping.

scaffold any of them (the flags work for every archetype):
  jaato-scaffold new client --transport in_process ...      # InProcessClient
  jaato-scaffold new client --transport ipc ...             # IPCClient (default)
  jaato-scaffold new client --transport ipc --recoverable . # IPCRecoveryClient
  jaato-scaffold new client --transport ws ...              # WSClient
  jaato-scaffold new client --transport ws --recoverable .  # WSRecoveryClient

  WHICH TURN METHOD — the question is whether the session is
  COMPLETION-GATED (does its profile declare completion_payload_schema?):

    method     settles on           returns                   session ends?
    ------------------------------------------------------------------
    ask        TURN_COMPLETED       the text of that turn     no
               session ends under it: raises SessionEnded unless the reason is clean
    stream     TURN_COMPLETED       the text, chunk by chunk  no
               session ends under it: yields what it had, then raises SessionEnded
    complete   SESSION_TERMINATED   AGENT_COMPLETED.payload   YES
               session ends under it: returns the payload; the ending is on Session.terminus

      WHICH turn method: ask/stream for a NON-GATED session (its turn IS the
      terminus; the turn event PROPOSES one, that agent's next status event
      CONFIRMS it, and SESSION_TERMINATED settles unconditionally — one rule
      parameterised by span since #1007, not first-of a pair), complete() for
      a COMPLETION-GATED one (an agent that ends a turn without
      signal_completion is re-prompted and keeps working, so the turn event
      fires mid-flight — jaato #767).  complete() also RETURNS the typed
      AGENT_COMPLETED payload; waiting on the terminal event alone tells you
      that a session ended and nothing about what it produced

  WHEN THE SESSION ENDS UNDER A TURN — a plain turn CAN end the
  session (a budget_control ceiling does exactly that), so this is
  not only a completion-gated concern:

    SessionEnded(reason, details)   raised by ask/stream when a
        terminal cut the turn short, and by all three on not_found.
        AgentError still wins where both apply — it is the richer type.
    clean endings                   client_request, natural, stopped
        An ALLOW-list: these return the turn normally.  A reason that
        does not exist yet raises rather than passing quietly.
    Session.terminus                (reason, details, session_ended)
        Recorded by all three verbs, and the only place the ending
        survives when complete() returns None.
    settle graces                   10.0s per agent, 1.0s per terminus
        The first asks 'is this agent going to take another turn';
        the second, 'did the daemon emit a terminal in the same
        breath as this turn event'.  The second expiring costs
        information, never correctness.

    Getting it wrong does not fail loudly.  complete() returns None when
    the profile declared no schema, the model never completed, or a
    budget ceiling stopped the session — three different endings with
    one return value, which is what Session.terminus above tells apart
    — and otherwise waits for a termination a
    conversational session may never reach.  Conversely a completed
    session is a session that ENDED: keep driving it and you replay a
    history whose tool_calls never got responses.
    Gated or not is decided in the profile, not here: see
    `explain completion` (the gate) and `explain plugin lifecycle`
    (signal_completion itself).

  TIMEOUTS — every clock between connect and a turn's terminus.
  They are not one knob, and they do not all live in the same place:

    default   where                                         settable via
    ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    120s      jaato.session(connect_timeout=)               facade
              connecting to (or autostarting) the daemon
              on expiry: ConnectionError — nothing was created
    5s        IPCClient.connect(timeout=)                   bare client only
              the same connect, on the BARE client
              on expiry: connect() returns False
    120s      IPCClient(autostart_timeout=)                 bare client only
              waiting for a daemon this client COLD-STARTED
              on expiry: the connect above fails
    60s       IPCClient.create_session(timeout=)            both
              the `session.new` confirmation — provider init included
              on expiry: SessionNotConfirmed — A SESSION MAY EXIST
    60s       jaato.session(session_timeout=)               facade
              the same `session.new` confirmation, from the facade
              on expiry: SessionNotConfirmed — A SESSION MAY EXIST
    none      Session.ask / .complete / .stream(timeout=)   facade
              ONE turn, caller-side
              on expiry: TurnTimeout — stops WAITING, not the session

    The facade and the bare client carry DIFFERENT connect defaults,
    deliberately: a cold daemon autostart takes ~30-60s, which the
    facade's default accounts for and the bare constructor's does not.
    A hand-rolled client that autostarts must pass its own.
    A `session.new` that times out is the one failure that may have
    LEFT A SESSION RUNNING — it has no idempotency key, so retrying
    makes a second one.  Raise it (session_timeout= on the facade,
    timeout= on create_session) before retrying; list_sessions().

data.does_not_terminate_on_its_own: without max_refusals the processor refuses, the agent re-claims completion, forever — seven refusals in 156 seconds, same two errors, no work in between, budget gone and no verdict (#768 rule 2).
data.retry_budget_is_budget_control: a blocked signal_completion is retried until either the processor's own max_refusals stops it blocking or the profile's budget_control crosses a degrade rung whose action is abort; there is no second attempts knob, and adding one to a driver is the wrong fix.  Declare NEITHER and the retry loop is unbounded (#947).  What max_refusals bounds is how many times THIS GATE may block, which is a different thing.

completion.text:
completion processors — the OUTPUT-side script hook (shared/completion_processors.py):

  WHAT: profile-declared Python that runs when the agent calls
  signal_completion, AFTER its payload passes completion_payload_schema.
  A `validate` that returns errors BLOCKS the completion and hands the
  agent a `validation_failed` result carrying every string, so it fixes
  and calls signal_completion again.  It is the framework's
  fix-until-it-passes loop.  The INPUT-side sibling is `explain
  prefetch` — read it first; this is the same shape at the other
  boundary.

  WHO OWNS signal_completion: the session-level lifecycle tools
  (shared/lifecycle_tools.py), wired by JaatoSession.configure() for
  every session — NOT a registry plugin, so it is not in `plugins:`
  and not in `explain plugins`.  `explain plugin lifecycle` has the
  tools and their gates.  What turns gating ON is one profile key:
  completion_payload_schema.  Without it signal_completion is not on
  the wire at all and the session just ends when the model stops —
  so a profile carrying completion_processors and no schema has a
  gate that can never run (`validate` reports that pair).

  THE OTHER GATE IS NOT A PROFILE KEY — it is the CLIENT.  A ROOT
  session keeps signal_completion for client_type api
  and HIDES it for chat, terminal, web, which expect the session to
  stay open for more turns.  So one profile completes under a
  headless driver and cannot complete under the TUI, and a persona
  that tells the model to signal is right in one and wrong in the
  other.  A SUBAGENT is unaffected: it keeps the tool whenever a
  schema is declared, whatever its parent's client is.

  TWO SHAPES OF A CORRECT FINISH, and a watcher must not read the
  second as a loop:
    one-shot     signal_completion(<the whole payload>)
    field-by-    prepare_completion(field_path, value)  × ~one per
      field      schema field, optionally query_completion to see what
                 is still pending, then signal_completion() with NO
                 args — the framework synthesizes from what accumulated
  Both are the protocol working.  The second exists for models that
  collapse to args={} when asked to compose a whole structured payload
  in one emission, and a correction pass after a processor refuses is
  normal.  So ~N prepare_completion calls for an N-field schema, plus a
  few, is expected; what a LOOP looks like is the same two errors with
  no work in between (see max_refusals below).  prepare_completion and
  query_completion exist only when a completion_payload_schema is
  declared — there is nothing to accumulate against otherwise.

  AUTHOR IT in two places:
    .jaato/profiles/<set>/<agent>.yaml   the wiring (fields below)
    <config_root>/scripts/processors/<f>.py   the module (or
                                     ~/.jaato/scripts/processors/<f>.py,
                                     daemon-global; same loader as
                                     prefetch scripts and reactors)

  WIRING (a `completion_processors:` list entry):
    script           str                   (required)
    output           Optional[str]         default None
    on_error         str                   default 'fail_completion'
    description      Optional[str]         default None
    phase            str                   default 'finalization'
    name             Optional[str]         default None
    max_refusals     Optional[int]         default None
    on_exhausted     str                   default 'allow'
    on_error → fail_completion|warn  phase → finalization|completeness  on_exhausted → allow|fail

  MODULE contract — one or both top-level callables:
    def render(payload, context) -> str | bytes
        content; written to the entry's `output:` template when it
        declares one, else logged for audit only.
    def validate(payload, context) -> ProcessorResult
        from jaato_sdk.cascade_authoring import ProcessorResult
        A dict of four channels (a bare list[str] is still accepted
        and read as all-errors):

      channel      blocks completion?        spends a refusal?
      errors       yes, per on_error         yes — one per CALL, not
                                             per message
      faults       once per session          never
      warnings     never                     never
      incomplete   never (gates is_complete  never
                   on a phase:completeness
                   processor)

    context = RenderContext: agent_params, workspace_path,
      config_root, env, session_id, registry, runtime, logger, and
      tool_calls — the paired ledger of every function_call and its
      response, for cross-checking a payload's claims against what
      the session ACTUALLY did.

  TWO WAYS TO CHECK A CLAIM, AND THE SECOND IS STRONGER.
    The ledger (`context.tool_calls`) proves the agent CALLED a tool.
    The filesystem proves the tool LEFT SOMETHING BEHIND — and that is
    the claim a downstream stage actually depends on.  A `validate` may
    read the workspace, so an agent that reports `output_file:` can be
    held to it:

      def validate(payload, context):
          out = Path(context.workspace_path) / payload['output_file']
          if not out.is_file():
              return {'errors': [f"{payload['output_file']} does not "
                                 f'exist — write it, then signal again']}
          if out.stat().st_size == 0:
              return {'errors': [f"{payload['output_file']} is empty"]}
          return {}

    That turns the payload into a VERIFIABLE contract between driver and
    agent rather than a report taken on trust, and it costs one stat().
    Two rules make it behave:
      - a path from the payload is MODEL-supplied.  Resolve it under
        workspace_path and reject one that escapes (`..`, an absolute
        path) — a processor runs with the session's own file access.
      - report the miss as `errors` (retryable — the agent can still
        write the file on a later turn), NOT as `faults`, which is for
        an environment the agent cannot fix.

  THE RETRY BUDGET IS budget_control.  A blocked completion is
  retried until the processor's own max_refusals stops it blocking,
  or the profile's budget_control crosses a degrade rung whose
  action is abort.  There is no second attempts knob, and adding
  one to a driver is the wrong fix (that PR was closed on finding
  this mechanism).  Declare NEITHER and the retry loop is
  UNBOUNDED — `limits` alone are observed, never enforced, so a
  ladder with an abort rung is what actually stops it (#947).

  THE TERMINUS A DRIVER WAITS ON IS NOT AGENT_COMPLETED.  An accepted
  signal_completion emits AgentCompletedEvent with the payload, but
  Session.complete() settles on the SESSION: first-of
  {SessionTerminatedEvent, TurnCompletedEvent + the settling status}.
  Both of those are emitted from ONE post-turn site, and that site is
  gated on a turn having RUN.  It used to be gated on a turn having
  been RECORDED in the usage ledger, which happens only when the
  provider reported tokens — so a turn whose provider reported NO
  usage did its work, delivered its payload, and emitted no terminal
  event at all, leaving the driver to wait out its own timeout with
  nothing logged on either side (#881).  The gate now reads a
  lifecycle counter, so a turn terminates because it ENDED rather
  than because it was billed.

  `echo` IS STILL WORTH A usage BLOCK, for a different reason now.
  The test double reports the spend it is TOLD to and none otherwise,
  so a harness built on it terminates fine and accounts for nothing:
  an empty consumption report, and a budget_control ceiling on
  `tokens` or `usd` fed zero that will never fire.  Declare one:

    plugin_configs:
      echo:
        usage: {prompt_tokens: 1000, output_tokens: 200}

  `jaato-scaffold validate` flags the omission (echo_reports_no_usage),
  and the session logs a WARNING naming the provider the first time a
  turn carries no tokens.  The framework's own conformance profiles
  all pass a usage block — except one, deliberately, which is what
  keeps the unmetered path exercised.

  THE LOOP DOES NOT TERMINATE ON ITS OWN.  Without `max_refusals`
  the processor refuses, the agent re-claims completion, and round
  it goes: an observed run spent SEVEN refusals in 156 seconds on
  the same two errors, with no work in between, and ended with its
  budget gone and no verdict.  Nothing upstream catches this —
  the completion-nudge budget bounds the opposite direction (an
  agent that stops WITHOUT signalling; `max_completion_nudges:`,
  default 2).  Declare a ceiling:

    completion_processors:
      - script: scripts/processors/acceptance.py
        name: acceptance
        max_refusals: 3
        on_exhausted: allow      # allow | fail

  on_exhausted: allow  lets the unfinished completion stand (errors
    downgraded to warnings) — right when something grades the run
    afterwards, because a FAIL verdict carries information and a
    BLOCKED arm carries none.
  on_exhausted: fail   keeps blocking — right when an unfinished
    completion is worse than none (it writes to a shared store, say).
  Both are real choices.  The counter lives on the framework's
  per-session LoadedProcessor, so a module-level global in your
  script is no longer the place for it.

  THE OTHER DIRECTION IS `max_completion_nudges` (#919).  Where
  `max_refusals` bounds how many times a processor may BLOCK a
  completion, this bounds how many times the framework re-prompts
  an agent that ended its loop without calling signal_completion
  at all, before giving up with NudgeExhausted:

    max_completion_nudges: 4      # profile top level; default 2

  Two is right for a strong tool-caller and is unchanged.  Raise
  it for a model that reliably does the work and unreliably
  reports it done — an audio tier that hands off, writes, narrates
  the write, and burns one of its two nudges on a redundant
  enter_tier has exactly one real attempt left.  Per TURN — every
  turn of a conversation gets the same allowance, rather than
  inheriting what an earlier turn spent (#934).  Positive integer
  (0 is refused — the give-up test is `fired >= max`, so a budget
  of 0 would report NudgeExhausted on sessions that completed
  cleanly).  Inherits child-override, else the
  minimum across parents.

  SEPARATE A WRONG ANSWER FROM AN ENVIRONMENT FAULT.  A missing
  acceptance script, an absent agent_param, a checks timeout: no fix
  the agent makes can clear those, so a retryable message about one
  burns the whole budget without ever producing a verdict.  Return
  them in `faults[]` — budget-exempt, and blocking only the single
  round-trip the agent needs to record the fault in its payload.

  NEVER RETURN [] ON A BROKEN GATE.  If your checking script exits
  non-zero with no output, the gate did not RUN — returning [] there
  waves the completion through on a check that never happened.  An
  error path returning the same value as success is the defect class
  this hook attracts most.  The framework holds the same line: a
  raise, a malformed return, a missing module and a failed write all
  BLOCK, spend no refusal, and are never waved through by
  exhaustion.

  WRITE THE STRINGS AS INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE RETRY, not as a report:
  they are read by a model about to try again.  Name the failure and
  what to do about it; the framework appends the attempts remaining.

  GENERATE ONE with those parts already right:
    jaato-scaffold new processor --name <n> --workspace DIR
  and see `explain archetype processor` for what it writes.

JAATO_CGROUPS_ROOT.scope_note: where the host delegated cgroup v2 subtree_control; one per host

JAATO_CONFIG_ROOT.scope_note: per-connection config search root; typed on the handshake, not the profile

JAATO_DAEMONIZED.description: internal — set by the daemonizer for its re-exec'd child; not an operator knob
JAATO_DAEMONIZED.scope_note: the daemon telling its own re-exec that it is the background copy

JAATO_EGRESS_NFT_ENFORCE.description: opt-in hard cgroup-nft egress enforcement (§5.11d-v2); needs a per-session cgroup + nft.  "1"/"true"/"yes"/"on" = best-effort, "strict" = deny the session when the gate cannot be installed
JAATO_EGRESS_NFT_ENFORCE.scope_note: nftables egress enforcement; a host firewall posture

JAATO_EPHEMERAL_TIMEOUT_S.description: seconds an ephemeral relay session may run before the daemon gives up (default 1800)
JAATO_EPHEMERAL_TIMEOUT_S.scope_note: the daemon's reaper deadline for relay sessions, applied to all of them

JAATO_IPC_EVENT_QUEUE_MAX.description: per-client IPC event-queue bound; past it the oldest lossy chunks drop (default 2048)
JAATO_IPC_EVENT_QUEUE_MAX.scope_note: how many events the daemon buffers per IPC client before it starts dropping lossy chunks; one bound per daemon, and a per-session value would be meaningless because the queue is owned by the transport, not by a session

JAATO_IPC_TRUST_PEER_PATHS.description: switch OFF the IPC peer check: act on any path a client names, unverified
JAATO_IPC_TRUST_PEER_PATHS.scope_note: switches OFF the IPC peer-entitlement check, so the daemon acts on whatever workspace / config_root a client names.  A property of the SOCKET -- one file, one set of principals reaching it -- and deliberately not per session: a session cannot be allowed to widen the transport's own trust posture, which is the reading --ws-unsafe-no-auth and JAATO_APPARMOR_COMPLAIN already get

JAATO_LOCK_HOLD_WARN_MS.description: ms SessionManager._lock may be held before LOCK_HELD_LONG is logged with the holder's stack (default 500; 0 off)
JAATO_LOCK_HOLD_WARN_MS.scope_note: milliseconds a profiled daemon lock (SessionManager._lock) may be held before its release is logged at WARNING with the holder's stack (#1452; default 500, 0 disables).  Host-scoped: the lock belongs to the daemon process, and its holders serve different sessions, so no one session could own the threshold

JAATO_PROVIDER_TRACE.description: debug — path of the provider request/response trace log (set via client config)
JAATO_PROVIDER_TRACE.scope_note: the incident in issue #775; now typed and validated

JAATO_REVIVE_PERSONA.description: a revived session's system prompt: persisted (default) or disk, which RE-RUNS prefetch scripts
JAATO_REVIVE_PERSONA.scope_note: revive posture of the daemon: reuse the session's persisted rendered prompt (default) or re-render it from disk, re-running the persona's prefetch scripts.  Cannot be a profile key -- it decides whether the persona is read at all (#787)

JAATO_REVIVE_PROFILE.description: a revived session's profile: persisted (default, frozen at creation) or disk (re-resolve now)
JAATO_REVIVE_PROFILE.scope_note: revive posture of the daemon: reuse the session's persisted resolved profile (default) or re-resolve the name from disk.  Self-referential as a profile key: the daemon would have to load the file to learn whether it may load the file (#787)

JAATO_RUNNER_ACK_TIMEOUT.description: seconds a dispatched runner RPC may go unacknowledged before the daemon reconciles it against the runner (0 disables)
JAATO_RUNNER_ACK_TIMEOUT.scope_note: seconds a dispatched runner RPC may go unacknowledged before the daemon reconciles it against the runner and fails it (#856).  A property of the daemon<->runner TRANSPORT, which is owned by the channel and not by a session -- the same reading JAATO_IPC_EVENT_QUEUE_MAX gets.  Sessions on one channel cannot disagree about it, because a pool slot serves several of them in turn through one RunnerRPCClient

JAATO_RUNNER_DISABLE_CONFINE.description: unsupported debug escape hatch: skip AppArmor self-confinement in the runner
JAATO_RUNNER_DISABLE_CONFINE.scope_note: disables runner self-confinement host-wide; deliberately NOT per session

JAATO_RUNNER_LOG_PATH.description: internal — set by the daemon per runner: runner log file path
JAATO_RUNNER_LOG_PATH.scope_note: daemon tells the runner subprocess where to log

JAATO_RUNNER_POOL_ENABLED.description: use the pre-warm runner pool (faster session bootstrap); false to always cold-spawn
JAATO_RUNNER_POOL_ENABLED.scope_note: pre-warm pool routing; a property of the daemon, not of one session

JAATO_RUNNER_POOL_MAX_SIZE.description: hard ceiling on total idle pre-warm slots incl. per-cascade reservations
JAATO_RUNNER_POOL_MAX_SIZE.scope_note: ceiling on the daemon's total warm slots, cascade reservations included; one memory budget per daemon, and a per-session value would be a lie about a shared pool

JAATO_RUNNER_POOL_SIZE.description: number of idle pre-warm runner slots to keep (raise for concurrent cascade fan-out)
JAATO_RUNNER_POOL_SIZE.scope_note: how many warm slots the daemon keeps; one number per daemon

JAATO_RUNNER_PROFILE.description: internal — set by the daemon per runner: profile to bootstrap the session with
JAATO_RUNNER_PROFILE.scope_note: daemon hands the runner the AppArmor profile name to self- confine to

JAATO_RUNNER_SELINUX_LABEL.description: internal — set by the daemon per runner: the SELinux context the exec put this runner in
JAATO_RUNNER_SELINUX_LABEL.scope_note: daemon tells a cold-spawned runner the SELinux context its exec transition entered, so it confirms instead of aa_change_profile

JAATO_RUNNER_SESSION_ID.description: internal — set by the daemon per runner: session id this runner serves
JAATO_RUNNER_SESSION_ID.scope_note: daemon hands the runner its session id

JAATO_RUNNER_UID_POLICY.description: which uid a root daemon runs each session's runner as -- daemon (default), peer (the IPC SO_PEERCRED uid) or workspace-owner (#1168)
JAATO_RUNNER_UID_POLICY.scope_note: which uid a ROOT daemon runs each session's runner as (#1168): daemon (default, no drop), peer (the IPC SO_PEERCRED uid) or workspace-owner.  A property of the daemon, never of a session: which accounts a runner may become is the operator's decision about the host, and a profile author must not be able to pick a uid.  Its CLI twin is `--runner-uid-policy`, which outranks it

JAATO_RUNNER_WORKSPACE.description: internal — set by the daemon per runner: session workspace root
JAATO_RUNNER_WORKSPACE.scope_note: daemon hands the runner its workspace path

JAATO_SESSION_LOG_DIR.description: per-session log directory; relative paths resolve against the workspace (default .jaato/logs)
JAATO_SESSION_LOG_DIR.scope_note: a per-session path with no typed key -- same shape as the trace incident

JAATO_TRACE_LOG.description: debug — path of the shared trace log plugins and servers append diagnostic lines to
JAATO_TRACE_LOG.scope_note: sibling of JAATO_PROVIDER_TRACE; typed together with it

JAATO_UMASK.description: octal umask for the daemon process, inherited by every runner it forks (e.g. 002 for a shared-group workspace)
JAATO_UMASK.scope_note: the octal umask of the daemon PROCESS, which every runner it forks inherits and so every file the agent writes (#1168).  `os.umask` is a process attribute and the daemon serves all of its sessions from one process, so a per-session value could not be applied without racing whatever turn is already running -- unimplementable rather than merely undesirable. Its CLI twin is `--umask`, which outranks it

JAATO_WORKSPACE_ROOT.description: internal — set by the framework per session: workspace root; read via session_context helpers
JAATO_WORKSPACE_ROOT.scope_note: the session's workspace; typed on the handshake and refused when relative (#742)

JAATO_WS_TOKEN.scope_note: the daemon's WS bearer token; one per listener, never per session

LOCATION.description: Vertex AI region for Google GenAI (e.g. us-central1 or global)
LOCATION.scope_note: the Vertex region -- connection identity with no google_genai knob

PROJECT_ID.description: GCP project ID for Google GenAI / Vertex AI
PROJECT_ID.scope_note: the GCP project -- connection identity with no google_genai knob

ENV_VALIDATE_CA.description: opt-in: warn at startup when REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / SSL_CERT_FILE point to missing files
ENV_VALIDATE_CA.scope_note: TLS trust configuration; a host posture

JAATO_APPARMOR_COMPLAIN.description: load AppArmor profiles in complain mode (logs denials, enforces nothing) -- a host-wide diagnostic
JAATO_APPARMOR_COMPLAIN.scope_note: kernel policy load mode; a host-wide diagnostic posture

JAATO_APP_CATEGORIES.description: comma-separated marketplace categories the application claims (app attribution)
JAATO_APP_CATEGORIES.scope_note: comma-separated marketplace categories the application claims; a property of the product, not of a conversation

JAATO_APP_NAME.description: display name of the application embedding jaato (app attribution)
JAATO_APP_NAME.scope_note: names the application embedding the framework; one app per deployment, and the per-session need is served by the provider knobs that outrank it

JAATO_APP_POWERED_BY.description: append "(powered by jaato)" to app attribution (default true)
JAATO_APP_POWERED_BY.scope_note: whether app attribution appends '(powered by jaato)'; a property of the product, not of a conversation

JAATO_APP_URL.description: the embedding application's site/repo URL (app attribution)
JAATO_APP_URL.scope_note: the embedding application's own site/repo, attributed upstream; one app per deployment

JAATO_APP_VERSION.description: the embedding application's own version string (app attribution)
JAATO_APP_VERSION.scope_note: the embedding application's own version; one app per deployment

JAATO_CREDENTIAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT.description: seconds to wait for another process refreshing a rotating OAuth credential (default 60)
JAATO_CREDENTIAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT.scope_note: seconds a caller waits for another process to finish refreshing a rotating OAuth credential before giving up (#683).  Host-scoped for the reason JAATO_RUNNER_ACK_TIMEOUT is: the thing being bounded is contention on a FILE, and the contenders are the daemon, its runner subprocesses and every pool slot -- several of which serve sessions that have no say in each other's timeouts.  A per-session value would also be incoherent, since the waiter and the holder are different sessions by construction

JAATO_DEFERRED_TOOLS.scope_note: tool-loop behaviour; a cheap model and an expensive one want opposite values in one sweep

JAATO_GRAPHICS_PROTOCOL.scope_note: forces the terminal graphics protocol; a property of the terminal, client-side

JAATO_LEDGER_INTEGRITY.scope_note: the ledger's tamper-evidence posture (sha256-chain | none). The env var is the TRANSPORT, not where an author writes it: the ledger is constructed before any profile resolves, so the typed block seeds this the way trace.ledger seeds LEDGER_PATH

JAATO_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN.scope_note: seconds before real expiry at which an OAuth access token is treated as stale and refreshed (#683).  Host-scoped because every process sharing one credential file must agree on when that file's token is stale: two sessions disagreeing would have the shorter-margin one repeatedly decline to refresh a token the other has already replaced, which is the desynchronisation the margin exists to prevent

JAATO_PARALLEL_TOOLS.scope_note: tool-loop behaviour; today one host-wide setting for every agent

env.text:
env vars read by the installed daemon + plugins (267 total, 244 documented)
  (commented = optional; descriptions come from `# env: ...` comments at the read site)

  scope (shared/env_scope.py — S session, H host, a ambient, i internal):
    186 session   a knob two sessions on one host may differ on — 153 have a typed key,
         33 do not (tiers: A=9 B=8 E=16). `explain env untyped`
     47 host      process/host-scoped — a per-session value would be a lie
     26 ambient   the host environment being READ, not a knob at all
      8 internal  one framework process handing a value to another

  TWO ROUTES SET THESE — the profile block wins:
    <workspace>/.env                     VAR=value           per-WORKSPACE  (lower)
    .jaato/profiles/<set>/<agent>.yaml   env: {VAR: value}   per-SESSION    (higher)
  The profile `env:` block:
    - outranks the workspace .env, per key
    - takes ${VAR} expansion + secret URIs (pass://, vault://, ...)
    - is applied verbatim — a relative path is resolved by its READER
    - refuses a SWITCH (1/true/off) in a path var — #775, at profile load
      Nothing rewrites the value on the way in, so WHERE a relative path
      lands is the reader's business, and readers differ:
        · the trace vars (JAATO_PROVIDER_TRACE / JAATO_TRACE_LOG) join theirs
          onto JAATO_WORKSPACE_ROOT, which the runner seeds per session — so a
          RELATIVE value gives each session its own file in its own workspace,
          and an ABSOLUTE one is fixed at the profile and shared by every
          session using it (jaato_sdk/trace.py _resolve_trace_file).
        · a reader that just open()s the value gets the runner process's cwd,
          which is NOT the workspace: the runner is forked into the daemon's
          cwd (core.py:1029 — the chdir promised at core.py:336 does not
          happen), and the subagent path can chdir it later, so it is not a
          thing to write a path against.  `${workspaceRoot}` / `${cwd}` are no
          help either: they expand daemon-side, before the session exists.
    - merges per KEY across `inherits:` (a child wins only the keys it sets)
    - is the ONLY route when the .env is not yours to write — jaato-eval writes
      each arm's .env itself (JAATO_PROFILE_SET and nothing else), so a task
      author cannot put anything there.

        env:
          JAATO_PROVIDER_TRACE: provider_trace.log    # one file per session

  A var with a TYPED key (the `→ typed:` line on its row below) has a
  better route than `env:`: the typed one is validated, and `env:` is
  not.  The two trace vars are the worked example in both directions —
  `env: {JAATO_PROVIDER_TRACE: 1}` is a valid str and wrote every
  session's trace to a file named `1` (#775).  BOTH routes refuse that
  now, and the typed block additionally checks the path's vocabulary:

        trace:
          provider_log: provider_trace.log   # same resolution, checked

  SUBSTITUTION — what a value may contain, and when it is resolved:

    resolved by expand_variables (daemon, at profile resolution):
      ${cwd}             the session's workspace root, else the resolving process's cwd
      ${workspaceRoot}   the workspace root detected from .git / .jaato
      ${jdtlsStateRoot}  the framework-managed jdtls state directory, a sibling of the workspace (Eclipse forbids it inside the project)
      ${HOME}            the resolving process's $HOME
      ${USER}            the resolving process's $USER
      ${ANY_ENV_VAR}     any process / session env var; an UNDEFINED name is left literal, and a literal ${...} in a path is created as a directory
      → honoured in: env:, plugin_configs:, trace:, and plugin configs that expand (lsp, webhook, web_fetch, service_connector, references)

    resolved by jaato_sdk.trace (the writer, per line):
      {agent}         the agent writing the line -- `main` for the main agent, `subagent_1`, `subagent_2`, ... for spawned subagents
      {agent_suffix}  `_subagent_1` for a subagent and EMPTY for the main agent -- what the implicit form appends, placeable anywhere in the path
      → honoured in: trace.session_log / trace.provider_log / trace.ledger and their env vars

    The two vocabularies are told apart by the `$`, and do NOT overlap:
    `${agent}` is an env var nobody sets; `{agent}` is the per-agent token.
    A `{token}` the framework does not know is REFUSED in `trace:` at profile
    load and reported by `validate` — unresolved, it becomes a literal directory.

data.doc: Agent has completed its task.

event AGENT_COMPLETED.text:
AGENT_COMPLETED   (agent.completed)
  direction : Server → Client
  domain    : Agent lifecycle
  class     : AgentCompletedEvent
  subscribe : event_types=["AgentCompletedEvent"]   (cascade_events / observer filters match the CLASS name)
  purpose   : Agent has completed its task.
  fields    :
    agent_id     : str
    completed_at : str
    success      : bool
    token_usage  : Optional[Dict[str, int]]
    turns_used   : Optional[int]
    error        : str
    payload      : Optional[Dict[str, Any]]

events.text:
event protocol — 169 typed events across 41 domains
  (S→C server→client, C→S client→server, S↔C bidirectional; wire value is the on-the-wire `type`. `explain event <NAME>` for detail)
  NOTE a cascade/observer subscription filters on the CLASS name (SessionTerminatedEvent),
       not on the member or the wire value — `cascade_events(event_types=[...])` and the daemon both
       compare type(event).__name__, so a wire value there matches nothing at all (#821).

  [Agent lifecycle]
    AGENT_COMPLETED       agent.completed       [S→C]
    AGENT_CREATED         agent.created         [S→C]
    AGENT_ERROR           agent.error           [S→C]
    AGENT_OUTPUT          agent.output          [S→C]
    AGENT_STATUS_CHANGED  agent.status_changed  [S→C]

  [Agent profiles]
    SESSION_PROFILES  session.profiles  [S→C]

  [Cascade stage settled]
    SLOT_SETTLED  slot.settled  [?]

  [Clarification flow]
    CLARIFICATION_BATCH           clarification.batch           [S→C]
    CLARIFICATION_BATCH_RESPONSE  clarification.batch_response  [C→S]
    CLARIFICATION_INPUT_MODE      clarification.input_mode      [S↔C]
    CLARIFICATION_QUESTION        clarification.question        [S↔C]
    CLARIFICATION_REQUESTED       clarification.requested       [S↔C]
    CLARIFICATION_RESOLVED        clarification.resolved        [S↔C]
    CLARIFICATION_RESPONSE        clarification.response        [C→S]

  [Client configuration]
    CLIENT_CONFIG  client.config  [C→S]

  [Client requests]
    COMMAND               command.execute       [C→S]
    COMMAND_LIST_REQUEST  command.list_request  [C→S]
    SEND_MESSAGE          message.send          [C→S]
    STOP                  session.stop          [C→S]

  [Client-side tool execution]
    TOOLS_REGISTER_CLIENT  tools.register_client  [C→S]
    TOOL_EXECUTE_REQUEST   tool.execute_request   [S→C]
    TOOL_EXECUTE_RESULT    tool.execute_result    [C→S]

  [Command list]
    COMMAND_LIST          command.list          [S→C]
    COMMAND_LIST_REFRESH  command.list_refresh  [S→C]

  [Connection lifecycle]
    CONNECTED     connected     [?]
    DISCONNECTED  disconnected  [?]   (no class — command/marker)

  [Context/token updates]
    BUDGET_RUNG_FIRED           budget.rung_fired           [S→C]
    CONTEXT_UPDATED             context.updated             [S→C]
    GC                          gc                          [S→C]
    GC_CONFIG                   gc.config                   [S→C]
    INCIDENT_RAISED             incident.raised             [S→C]
    INSTRUCTION_BUDGET_UPDATED  instruction_budget.updated  [S→C]
    TURN_COMPLETED              turn.completed              [S→C]
    TURN_PROGRESS               turn.progress               [S→C]

  [Event subscription notifications]
    EVENTS_SUBSCRIBED  events.subscribed  [S→C]

  [External events]
    EVENT_EXTERNAL  event.external  [C→S]

  [File staging into a workspace]
    WORKSPACE_FILES_SEARCH_REQUEST  workspace.files.search         [C→S]
    WORKSPACE_FILES_SEARCH_RESULT   workspace.files.search_result  [S→C]
    WORKSPACE_FILES_STAGED          workspace.files.staged         [S→C]
    WORKSPACE_FILES_STAGE_REQUEST   workspace.files.stage_request  [C→S]
    WORKSPACE_FILE_CONTENT          workspace.file.content         [S→C]
    WORKSPACE_FILE_FETCH_REQUEST    workspace.file.fetch           [C→S]

  [HandoffGate events]
    GATES_SNAPSHOT  gates.snapshot  [?]
    GATE_ANNOUNCED  gate.announced  [?]
    GATE_RELEASED   gate.released   [?]

  [History]
    HISTORY               history               [S↔C]
    HISTORY_PAGE          history.page          [S→C]
    HISTORY_PAGE_REQUEST  history.page.request  [C→S]
    HISTORY_REQUEST       history.request       [S↔C]

  [Identity at connect (#1074)]
    TICKET_BIND_REQUEST    ticket.bind           [C→S]

persona_guidance: use `gh` (and `git` over https) for GitHub work
never print or echo the token
on a 401, report it — do not run `gh auth login` (there is nothing on disk to repair)

app_reference.how: the daemon grants the names it resolved from app:// and these surfaces keep exactly those names

scrub.mcp: never granted; an MCP server gets no GitHub token

data.token_delivery: GH_TOKEN reaches the session as a literal in the workspace .env / profile env:, or as GH_TOKEN=app://github resolved by the daemon per spawn (#1226)

gh.text:
using `gh` / `git` with a per-user token (#1228):

  GH_TOKEN reaches a session two ways — a literal in the workspace
  .env / a profile's env:, or `GH_TOKEN=app://github`, which the daemon
  resolves to the real token at every spawn (#1226; cascade, wake and
  revived sessions get it too, and nothing resolved is persisted).
  Once it is there, three things must line up:

  1. THE SECRET SCRUB.
     GH_TOKEN is in the default scrub set: True.
     - app://github: nothing to do.  The daemon grants the names it
       resolved, and cli and interactive_shell keep exactly
       those names through the scrub.  A bind or unbind in the web
       client takes effect on the next command.
     - a literal token is scrubbed like any other secret.  Exempt it
       on the surfaces that run the model's shell:

       plugin_configs:
         cli: {scrub_secret_env: [default, "!GH_TOKEN"]}
         interactive_shell: {scrub_secret_env: [default, "!GH_TOKEN"]}

     mcp is never granted: an MCP server gets no GitHub token.

  2. NON-INTERACTIVE DEFAULTS, in the session env (profile env: or the
     workspace .env), so a missing credential is an error the model
     READS rather than a prompt nobody answers:

       env:
         GH_PROMPT_DISABLED: "1"
         GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: "0"

  3. PERSONA GUIDANCE (.jaato/agents/<name>.md):
       - use `gh` (and `git` over https) for GitHub work;
       - never print or echo the token;
       - on a 401, report it rather than running `gh auth login` —
         there is nothing on disk for the agent to repair.

  See the `gh` example in the web examples, and
  docs/design/per-user-github-credentials.md §7.

daemon-side, so it applies when the client died: max_orphan_seconds defaults to 900s, max_session_seconds is opt-in; 0 disables either
