    [disc] list_endpoints(service, filter_method=..., filter_path=..., filter_tag=...)
           List available endpoints from a discovered service or schema directory. Returns method, path, summary, and tags for each endpoint.
    [disc] get_endpoint_schema(service, method, path)
           Get the full request/response schema for a specific endpoint. Returns parameters, request body schema, and response schemas.
    [disc] call_service(service=..., url=..., method, path=..., endpoint=..., query=..., headers=..., body=..., auth=..., timeout=..., truncate_at=..., insecure=..., no_proxy=..., save_to=...)
           Execute an HTTP request. Can use a discovered service (with auth and base URL) or a raw URL. Request body is validated against schema if available. Response is validated and truncated if too large. The response is bulk content: when you are scanning it for something specific, call grep_mode_start(pattern) first to have these responses filtered to matching lines (with context) instead of returned in full — this cuts context cost. grep_mode_stop restores full responses.
    [disc] preview_request(service=..., url=..., method, path=..., query=..., headers=..., body=..., auth=...)

           schema (object, required):
             method*             string
             path*               string
             base_url            string
             summary             string
             parameters          array
             request_body        object
             responses           object
             (* = required within this object)

           Configure authentication for a discovered service, so later call_service(service=...) calls carry it. Credentials are NEVER passed here: every field below names an ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE the value is read from at request time. The fields `auth` needs depend on its `type`: apiKey -> in ('header'|'query'), name (the header or query-param name), value_env; bearer -> token_env; basic -> username_env, password_env; oauth2_client -> token_url, client_id_env, client_secret_env, and optionally scope; none -> nothing else. Example: {"type": "apiKey", "in": "header", "name": "PRIVATE-TOKEN", "value_env": "GITLAB_TOKEN"}.

             type*               string  one of: none, apiKey, bearer, basic, oauth2_client   Which scheme — decides which other fields apply
             in                  string  one of: header, query   apiKey: where to put the key
             name                string   apiKey: header or query-param name, e.g. PRIVATE-TOKEN
             value_env           string   apiKey: env var holding the key
             token_env           string   bearer: env var holding the token
             username_env        string   basic: env var holding the username
             password_env        string   basic: env var holding the password
             token_url           string   oauth2_client: token endpoint URL
             client_id_env       string   oauth2_client: env var holding the client id
             client_secret_env   string   oauth2_client: env var holding the client secret
             scope               string   oauth2_client: requested scope (optional)
             (* = required within this object)

data.description: Plugin for spawning subagents with specialized tool configurations.

tools.description: DELEGATE work to a subagent that runs IN PARALLEL / IN THE BACKGROUND. Use this to run CONCURRENT tasks, OFFLOAD work, or have a HELPER agent handle specialized operations while you continue with other work.
tools.name: spawn_subagent

agent.description: Name of an agent definition (parameterized prompt from .jaato/agents/). Provides the subagent's system instructions. Use with 'profile' for runtime config, or alone to inherit the parent's runtime config.

agent_params.description: Parameter values for the agent's {{param}} placeholders. Only used when 'agent' is specified.

context.description:
Optional context to provide to the subagent. Can be either:
- A string: Simple text context
- An object with structured context:
  - files: {path: content} - relevant file contents
  - findings: [list of facts/conclusions]
  - notes: free-form guidance

TOKEN ECONOMY: Be selective about what you share:
- Share only content RELEVANT to the subagent's specific task
- For large files, share only the relevant sections/functions
- Prefer file PATHS over full content when the subagent can read them
- Use 'findings' to summarize insights instead of raw data
- Remember: every token shared reduces the subagent's working space

files.description: Relevant file content: {path: content}. Share only sections relevant to the task, or just paths if the subagent can read them.

name.description: Descriptive name for the subagent (e.g., 'bug_fixer', 'code_reviewer', 'file_analyzer'). Use this when creating inline agents without a profile. If using a profile, this parameter is optional and the profile name will be used.

profile.description: REQUIRED. Name of a runtime profile (model, plugins, permissions). Use list_subagent_profiles to see available profiles. The profile decides which tools the subagent has; a profile may also bind its own persona via `default_agent`, so naming the profile alone is usually enough. The reserved value 'inherit' spawns a subagent from a frozen snapshot of YOUR OWN profile at this moment — your plugins (minus spawn_subagent, so it cannot itself spawn) and your system instructions — for a helper that behaves like you.

server.description: Optional: name of a remote peer server to run the subagent on. When specified, the subagent is delegated to the remote server instead of running locally. Use the environment tool's cluster topology to see available servers and their capabilities. NOTE: 'profile' is resolved by the PEER, but the values listed for it here are this server's own profiles (#1052) — a peer-only profile name must also be declared locally for the call to satisfy the schema.

task.description: The task or prompt to send to the subagent. Be specific about what you want the subagent to accomplish.

tools.description: Send a message to a running subagent for guidance or course correction. Use this for:
tools.name: send_to_subagent

message.description: Message to inject into the subagent's queue. Will be processed at the next yield point (after tool execution or model response).

subagent_id.description: ID of the active subagent session (returned by spawn_subagent). Use list_active_subagents to see available sessions.

tools.description: Close an active subagent session when the task is complete.
tools.name: close_subagent

tools.description: Cancel a running subagent, stopping its current operation immediately.

tools.description: List currently active subagent sessions with detailed status information.
tools.name: list_active_subagents

tools.description: List available subagent profiles. Use this to see what specialized subagents are configured and their capabilities.
tools.name: list_subagent_profiles

config.description: Whether renderTemplateToFile accepts an inline 'template' string.  false: only catalog templates (template_id) render, and the parameter is removed from the tool's schema.  With no free-form write tool on the profile (no writeNewFile/updateFile, cli, notebook, interactive_shell), a catalog template is then the only way to create a file.  Read per session: a subagent's own block governs it.

config.description: Output-path routing, declared by the profile, in the same shape `template_routing.yaml` carries at its top level: {'output_path_routing': [{'glob': '**/*.java', 'prefix': 'src/main/java'}, ...]}.  Rules are first-match-wins on `PurePath.match`; an empty prefix means match-and-leave-alone; prepending is idempotent.  When this key is PRESENT it IS the configuration and NO `template_routing.yaml` is read — not the config_root tier, not the workspace tier; present-and-empty declares that this profile routes nothing.  Absent keeps the file search.  Prefer it over the file: routing decides where generated files land, and `.jaato/profiles/**` is apparmor write-denied to the runner while the file tier is reachable from the workspace.
config.name: file_conventions

data.description: Plugin for template-based file generation.

derivation: template_id = "tpl_" + the first 8 hex digits (lowercase) of SHA-256 over the template's name, UTF-8 encoded
the name is the template's index name: the `name` of its entry in the catalog's index.json, or the file's basename for a template discovered at runtime
a pure function of the name: no session, workspace or configuration enters it, so it is stable across sessions and deployments
outside a session: `from jaato_sdk.templates import template_id`

tools.description: **PREFERRED OVER MANUAL CODING**: Render a template with variable substitution and write the result to a file. When a template exists for your task (use listAvailableTemplates to discover them), you MUST use this tool instead of writing code manually. Templates ensure consistency and reduce errors. Supports BOTH Jinja2 and Mustache/Handlebars syntax (auto-detected). Jinja2: {{name}}, {% if %}, {% for %}, {{ name | filter }}. Mustache: {{name}}, {{#items}}...{{/items}}, {{^empty}}...{{/empty}}, {{.}}. Provide either 'template' for inline content or 'template_id' for a registered template.
tools.name: renderTemplateToFile

output_path.description: OPTIONAL — defaults to the template's declared // Output: directive (substituted with your `variables`). When using `template_id`, omit this field unless you specifically need to redirect the output away from the template's canonical location. When using inline `template` OR when the template has no `// Output:` directive, you must supply this. NEVER include unsubstituted `{` or `}` placeholders.

overwrite.description: Allow overwriting existing file. Default is false.

template.description: Inline template string. Mutually exclusive with 'template_id'.

template_id.description: Opaque template identifier (e.g. 'tpl_a8f0e2b1') obtained from the 'id' field of a listAvailableTemplates response entry. Resolved internally to the template file. Mutually exclusive with 'template'. Do NOT pass human template filenames (e.g. 'Entity.java.tpl') — the framework hashes those at the LLM boundary to keep tool calls grounded in the listed catalog rather than training-distribution priors.

tools.description: **CHECK THIS BEFORE WRITING CODE**: List all templates available in this session. If a template exists for your task, you MUST use renderTemplateToFile instead of writing code manually. Shows both standalone templates (from referenced directories) and embedded templates (extracted from documentation). Each entry carries a stable opaque 'id' (e.g. 'tpl_a8f0e2b1') — pass this id to renderTemplateToFile and listTemplateVariables. The human template filename is reported on 'source_path' for human audit only; never pass it as a tool argument.
tools.name: listAvailableTemplates

tools.description: Validate a template index JSON file against the expected schema. Checks for required top-level fields, per-entry required fields, valid syntax and origin values, variable format, and optionally whether source paths exist on disk.
tools.name: validateTemplateIndex

path.description: Path to a template index JSON file to validate.

tools.description: List all variables required by a template, with structural type info for each one. Call this before renderTemplateToFile to know exactly what variables to provide AND what shape each variable needs.
tools.name: listTemplateVariables

template_id.description: Opaque template identifier (e.g. 'tpl_a8f0e2b1') obtained from the 'id' field of a listAvailableTemplates response entry. Do NOT pass human template filenames — see listAvailableTemplates description.

rules: an index entry may carry `variable_descriptions`: an object {variable name: description text}, beside `variables`
listTemplateVariables adds `description` to each variable that has one; a variable with none is returned as before (name, kind, ...)
a description naming a variable the template does not use is ignored by listTemplateVariables; validateTemplateIndex warns when the name is missing from the entry's `variables`
validateTemplateIndex refuses a non-object, a non-string or blank description; at load a malformed entry is dropped, never the template

plugin template.text:
plugin: template
  Plugin for template-based file generation.
  kind=tool  tier=runner
  tools:
    [disc] renderTemplateToFile(output_path=..., template_id=..., template=..., variables, overwrite=...)
           **PREFERRED OVER MANUAL CODING**: Render a template with variable substitution and write the result to a file. When a template exists for your task (use listAvailableTemplates to discover them), you MUST use this tool instead of writing code manually. Templates ensure consistency and reduce errors. Supports BOTH Jinja2 and Mustache/Handlebars syntax (auto-detected). Jinja2: {{name}}, {% if %}, {% for %}, {{ name | filter }}. Mustache: {{name}}, {{#items}}...{{/items}}, {{^empty}}...{{/empty}}, {{.}}. Provide either 'template' for inline content or 'template_id' for a registered template.
    [disc] listAvailableTemplates()
           **CHECK THIS BEFORE WRITING CODE**: List all templates available in this session. If a template exists for your task, you MUST use renderTemplateToFile instead of writing code manually. Shows both standalone templates (from referenced directories) and embedded templates (extracted from documentation). Each entry carries a stable opaque 'id' (e.g. 'tpl_a8f0e2b1') — pass this id to renderTemplateToFile and listTemplateVariables. The human template filename is reported on 'source_path' for human audit only; never pass it as a tool argument.
    [disc] validateTemplateIndex(path)
           Validate a template index JSON file against the expected schema. Checks for required top-level fields, per-entry required fields, valid syntax and origin values, variable format, and optionally whether source paths exist on disk.
    [disc] listTemplateVariables(template_id)
           List all variables required by a template, with structural type info for each one. Call this before renderTemplateToFile to know exactly what variables to provide AND what shape each variable needs.
  note: [core] tools are in the model's INITIAL schema; [disc] are DEFERRED — the model reaches them by calling list_tools / get_tool_schemas (introspection is always core, so they're never lost), OR add `template(preload)` to a profile's plugins to force ALL of this plugin's tools eager.
  config (plugin_configs.template.*):
    allow_inline_template  bool          Whether renderTemplateToFile accepts an inline 'template' string.  false: only catalog templates (template_id) render, and the parameter is removed from the tool's schema.  With no free-form write tool on the profile (no writeNewFile/updateFile, cli, notebook, interactive_shell), a catalog template is then the only way to create a file.  Read per session: a subagent's own block governs it.  (default True)
    file_conventions       dict          Output-path routing, declared by the profile, in the same shape `template_routing.yaml` carries at its top level: {'output_path_routing': [{'glob': '**/*.java', 'prefix': 'src/main/java'}, ...]}.  Rules are first-match-wins on `PurePath.match`; an empty prefix means match-and-leave-alone; prepending is idempotent.  When this key is PRESENT it IS the configuration and NO `template_routing.yaml` is read — not the config_root tier, not the workspace tier; present-and-empty declares that this profile routes nothing.  Absent keeps the file search.  Prefer it over the file: routing decides where generated files land, and `.jaato/profiles/**` is apparmor write-denied to the runner while the file tier is reachable from the workspace.  (default {})
  template_id (what listAvailableTemplates reports and renderTemplateToFile / listTemplateVariables accept):
    - template_id = "tpl_" + the first 8 hex digits (lowercase) of SHA-256 over the template's name, UTF-8 encoded
    - the name is the template's index name: the `name` of its entry in the catalog's index.json, or the file's basename for a template discovered at runtime
    - a pure function of the name: no session, workspace or configuration enters it, so it is stable across sessions and deployments
    - outside a session: `from jaato_sdk.templates import template_id`
  variable descriptions (catalog index.json):
    - an index entry may carry `variable_descriptions`: an object {variable name: description text}, beside `variables`
    - listTemplateVariables adds `description` to each variable that has one; a variable with none is returned as before (name, kind, ...)
    - a description naming a variable the template does not use is ignored by listTemplateVariables; validateTemplateIndex warns when the name is missing from the entry's `variables`

plugin todo.text:
plugin: todo
  Plugin that provides plan registration and progress tracking.
  kind=tool  tier=runner
  tools:
    [core] createPlan(title, steps)
           Step 1: Register a new execution plan with ordered steps. Think carefully before calling - only propose plans you can actually achieve with available tools. IMPORTANT: Before including any tool in a step, verify that tool is available and you are allowed to use it. Each step must be specific and actionable. After calling this, you MUST call startPlan to confirm the plan before executing steps.
    [core] startPlan(message=...)
           Step 2: Confirm the plan before beginning execution. This MUST be called after createPlan and BEFORE any setStepStatus calls. If the plan is rejected: call completePlan with status='cancelled', do NOT create another plan and retry.
    [core] setStepStatus(step_id, status, result=..., error=...)
           Step 3: Update the status of a step. Can only be called AFTER startPlan has been called. Use this to report progress as you work.
           status               string  one of: in_progress, completed, failed, skipped
    [core] getPlanStatus(plan_id=...)
           Query current plan state and progress. Can be called at any time.
    [core] completePlan(status, summary=...)
           Step 4: Mark the plan as finished. Use 'completed' or 'failed' only if the plan was started. Use 'cancelled' if the user rejected startPlan.
           status               string  one of: completed, failed, cancelled
    [core] addStep(description, after_step_id=...)
           Add a new step to an existing plan during execution. Use this when you discover missing steps, need a corrective action after a failure, or realize additional work is needed. ALWAYS prefer this over recreating the plan with createPlan. Can only be called AFTER startPlan has been called.
    [core] addDependentStep(step_id, depends_on, provides=...)
           Add a cross-agent dependency to an EXISTING step in your plan. The step will be BLOCKED until ALL dependencies complete, then auto-unblocks.
    [core] completeStepWithOutput(step_id, output, result=...)
           Complete a step AND pass structured data to tasks depending on it. This is how subagents report results back to parent agents.
    [core] getBlockedSteps(plan_id=...)
           See which of your steps are waiting on other agents.
  commands (typed directly in the TUI, not via the model):
    plan
           Show current or most recent plan status
  config (plugin_configs.todo.*):
    storage_type           string        one of: 'memory', 'file', 'hybrid'  Storage backend type  (default 'memory')
    initial_plan_name      string        Id of a predefined plan at <config_root>/plans/<id>.yaml.  The session that declares it starts with that plan active, is told so in its system prompt, and does not see createPlan.  An id, not a path.  A missing or malformed plan refuses the session.

  initial_plan_name names an authored plan FILE at <config_root>/plans/<id>.yaml
  (mirrors TodoPlan.to_dict()) — its shape:
    title                required  Plan summary — a non-empty string.
    steps                required  A non-empty list; each entry is a mapping.
    steps[].description  required  What the step does — a non-empty string.
    started              optional  Defaults to true: the authored file is the approval startPlan otherwise asks for.  Write started: false to make the agent confirm the plan first.
    context              optional  Free-form mapping; initial_plan_name is recorded in it.
    (full field table — sequence / validation_required / depends_on / …: the todo plugin README)

data.shrink: drops idle runners only: never-served ones above the floor first (newest first), then the stalest reservations and served runners of the least recently used posture while over the ceiling; a runner serving a session finishes it

sizing_signals.pool_acquire_miss_total: sessions found no warm runner and cold-spawned: raise the size

data.start_with_flags: python -m jaato_server --daemon --pool-size N [--pool-max M]  (also --web-socket, --restart); each flag outranks its env knob

startup_knobs.meaning: floor: unreserved idle runners any arriving session may take
ceiling: total idle runners, cascade reservations included
whether sessions are routed to the pool at all

data.who_may: the daemon's own uid or root, read from the IPC socket's SO_PEERCRED; never from the request

pool.text:
the pre-warm runner pool, and resizing it without a restart:

  Sessions take a warm runner from the pool instead of cold-
  spawning one.  The FLOOR is how many never-served idle runners
  are kept (a runner that served fits only that session's
  confinement posture, so it sits on top of the floor); the
  CEILING bounds all idle runners, cascade reservations and
  served runners included (each is 129-187 MB).

  AT STARTUP
    JAATO_RUNNER_POOL_SIZE      default 2: floor: unreserved idle runners any arriving session may take
    JAATO_RUNNER_POOL_MAX_SIZE  default 2 x pool size: ceiling: total idle runners, cascade reservations included
    JAATO_RUNNER_POOL_ENABLED   default true: whether sessions are routed to the pool at all
    This shell's environment: JAATO_RUNNER_POOL_SIZE=(unset), JAATO_RUNNER_POOL_MAX_SIZE=(unset), JAATO_RUNNER_POOL_ENABLED=(unset)
    (a daemon started elsewhere may differ; ask it, below)
    Or on the start command: --daemon --pool-size N [--pool-max M]
    (also with --web-socket or --restart).  Each flag outranks its
    env knob and leaves the other one alone; a foreground start
    (--ipc-socket alone) takes the env knobs, because there the
    flags resize the running daemon instead.

  ON A RUNNING DAEMON (no restart, no session unloaded)
    python -m jaato_server --pool-size N [--pool-max M]   resize and print
    python -m jaato_server --status            prints a pool: line
    pool.status / pool.resize <target> [<max>]   at the TUI prompt,
        or rich_client.py --cmd "pool.resize 6" (no --session needed)
    IPCClient.pool_status() / resize_pool(target, max)   from code
    Needs a daemon speaking protocol 1.35+; an older one is refused by the
    SDK rather than left to ignore the request.

  WHO MAY  the daemon's own account or root, read from the IPC
    socket's SO_PEERCRED, never from the request.  A WS connection
    has no OS account and is refused.

  REFUSALS (PoolStatusEvent.category)
    not_authorized   the connection is not the daemon's own account or root, or carries no OS account (WS, Windows)
    invalid_request  a size that is not a non-negative integer
    no_pool          the daemon runs without a runner pool

  GROWING  wakes the replenish loop; forking starts at once.
  SHRINKING  drops IDLE runners only: never-served ones above the
    floor first (newest first), then, while over the ceiling, the
    stalest reservations and served runners of the least recently
    used posture.  A runner serving a session finishes it.
  CEILING  a chosen max is kept (clamped up to the floor); a
    derived one (2 x floor) follows the floor.
  RESTART  --restart keeps the resized values; they outrank the
    env knobs from then on.  The answer says when that write failed.

  SIZING SIGNALS (counters on PoolStatusEvent.telemetry)
    pool_acquire_miss_total               sessions found no warm runner and cold-spawned: raise the size
    pool_replenish_ceiling_blocked_total  the ceiling stopped a refill: raise the max
    pool_stale_reservation_evicted_total  a cascade's warm runner was spent at the ceiling: raise the max
    pool_posture_miss_total               a session found only warm runners of another confinement posture and no fresh one: raise the size

data.agent_params_are_not_secret: agent_params are substituted into the persona, so anything put there reaches the model in its system prompt AND is persisted with the session (the rendered persona is stored so a revive restores it instead of re-running this script -- issue #787).  Pass credentials via profile env: with a pass:// / vault:// URI, which stays unresolved on disk and is resolved daemon-side at spawn.

context_attr_notes.runtime: the session's JaatoRuntime — ledger, registered providers
context_attr_notes.session_id: None when the session is not daemon-attached

data.runs_once: once per session, at session-prep.  A revived session restores the rendered prompt rather than re-running this script; JAATO_REVIVE_PERSONA=disk opts back into re-running it, so a side-effecting prefetch should be idempotent.

prefetch.text:
prefetch scripts — deterministic per-agent session-start behaviour
(dynamic-instruction `{{!py:...}}` expansion; shared/dynamic_instructions.py):

  WHAT: a persona placeholder that runs a Python script at session-prep
  (configure-time) and injects the returned string into the system prompt
  BEFORE the model's first turn — a deterministic, no-model-round-trip way
  to seed per-agent session-start context (fetched data, computed config,
  mandatory pre-reads).

  AUTHOR IT in two files:
    .jaato/agents/<name>.md          persona — write the placeholder
    <config_root>/scripts/<f>.py     the script (or ~/.jaato/scripts/<f>.py,
                                     daemon-global; same loader as reactors)

  DIRECTIVE forms (in the persona .md):
    {{!py:scripts/<f>.py a b}}    MANDATORY — a render() failure raises
        PrefetchError + aborts session-prep (the model must NOT start
        without this content).
    {{!py?:scripts/<f>.py ...}}   OPTIONAL — best-effort: a failure DROPS
        the placeholder instead of aborting.  (A script may also return a
        string starting with '[prefetch error: ...]' for a soft failure.)

  SCRIPT contract:
    def render(context, args) -> str
      args    = whitespace-split tokens after the script name.
      context = RenderContext, every attribute of it:
        session — the owning JaatoSession: session.workspace_path, session.history, ...
        runtime — the session's JaatoRuntime — ledger, registered providers
        registry — registry.get_plugin('<name>') to reach a plugin
        workspace_path
        config_root
        agent_params — the agent's params dict
        env — os.environ snapshot
        logger
        tool_calls — completion-time only; [] for input-side prefetch
        session_id — None when the session is not daemon-attached


  NEVER PASS A CREDENTIAL AS AN agent_param.  They are substituted
  into the persona, so they already reach the model in its system
  prompt — and the rendered persona is PERSISTED with the session
  (a revive restores it rather than re-running this script; #787).
  Secrets belong in the profile's `env:` as a pass:// / vault:// URI,
  which stays unresolved on disk and is resolved daemon-side.

  RUNS ONCE, at session-prep.  A revived session restores the
  rendered prompt instead of re-running the script; the operator can
  opt back into re-rendering with JAATO_REVIVE_PERSONA=disk, which
  re-runs render() against the session's ORIGINAL agent_params.  So
  a prefetch with side effects (fetching, writing a file, taking a
  lock) should be idempotent.

  WORKED EXAMPLE: shared/plugins/subagent/README.md -> prefetch_kyc_aml.py
  (a full persona placeholder + render() pulling plugin data into the prompt).

data.name: plugins

data.description: NOT a profile-file key — derived from plugins: — write `todo(preload)`.  DERIVED from `(preload)` annotations in `plugins` during parsing — not set directly.
data.name: preloaded_plugins

data.description: NOT a profile-file key — derived from plugins: — write `memory(tools:[a,b])`.  Per-plugin tool allow-lists (plugin -> [tool names to expose]); every other tool that plugin ships is dropped from this session's wire + grammar. Absent plugin = all its tools. Keep in sync with the persona's referenced tools.

data.description: Per-plugin config overrides (plugin name -> config dict), e.g. plugin_configs.<provider>.api_params / .extra_body, plugin_configs.permission.policy.
data.name: plugin_configs

data.description: DEPRECATED — use agents (.jaato/agents/<name>.md) instead; an `--agent`'s rendered markdown replaces this. Profiles should carry runtime config only.
data.name: system_instructions

data.description: Agent definition (.jaato/agents/<name>.md) whose persona this profile spawns with when the caller names no `agent`. A profile supplies plugins, an agent supplies instructions — this binds the two so `spawn_subagent(profile=...)` alone yields a subagent that has both. An explicit `agent=` wins.
data.name: default_agent

data.description: Drop framework-injected instruction layers from the system prompt (plugin + agent instructions always kept).  `true` drops the disk BASE layer (.jaato/instructions/*.md) AND the framework constants (task-completion, parallel guidance, turn-summary); the security untrusted-content boundary and the AI disclosure (EU AI Act Art. 50(1)) are kept.  A dict gives granular control over the four pieces, e.g. `{disk: true, constants: true, security: false}` (absent key = keep); dropping `security` or `disclosure` is a posture change and is announced at WARNING.  Saves ~3-5k tokens/turn for narrow goal-focused agents.  Default False.  Normalized to a canonical frozenset of piece names in __post_init__.
data.name: suppress_base_instructions

data.description: Model override (uses the parent's model if unset). Silently ignored when model_tiers is non-empty.
data.name: model

data.description: Provider override (e.g. anthropic, nebius, vllm). A profile binds exactly one provider + model.
data.name: provider

data.description: How many times the framework re-prompts a session that ended without calling signal_completion before giving up (NudgeExhausted). Per turn. None = the framework default, 2. Raise it for a model that reliably does the work and unreliably reports it done (audio models routinely burn a nudge on a redundant enter_tier). Positive integer; the sibling of a processor's max_refusals.
data.name: max_completion_nudges

data.description: Prompt-cache defaults, cross-provider. {enabled: auto|true|false, ttl: 5m|1h, history: bool}. 'auto' leaves the provider's own default alone and is a no-op on a provider that cannot cache. plugin_configs.<provider> overrides this for mechanism-specific tuning (more specific wins).
data.name: cache

data.description: Diagnostic trace-log paths: {session_log, provider_log, ledger}. Typed sibling of the JAATO_TRACE_LOG / JAATO_PROVIDER_TRACE / LEDGER_PATH env vars, which stay the lower-precedence default (this block outranks them). Absolute = one shared file; relative = one file per session, resolved against the workspace. Refuses a switch written into a path field -- `env: {JAATO_PROVIDER_TRACE: '1'}` is a valid str and wrote every session's trace to a file named `1` (#775).
data.name: trace

data.allowed: risk_class: minimal | limited | high (most-restrictive-wins across inherits)  |  keys: annex_iii, disclosure_text, intended_purpose, interacts_with_persons, provider, risk_class  |  provider: {name, contact}  |  absent = undeclared
data.description: What this application declares about itself under the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689): {intended_purpose, risk_class: minimal|limited|high, annex_iii, provider: {name, contact}, interacts_with_persons, disclosure_text}.  Declared, never inferred -- whether a use is high-risk is the provider's own determination (Art. 6(4)).  `validate` escalates its warnings to errors under risk_class: high; the disclosure piece reads provider.name and interacts_with_persons (Art. 50(1)).  risk_class inherits most-restrictive-wins, the other fields child-replaces.  Absent = undeclared (validated as minimal, documented as unknown).
data.name: regulatory

data.description: How long this session's records are kept and whether they carry tamper evidence (EU AI Act Arts. 12, 19, 26(6)): {retention_days, conversation_retention_days, integrity: none|sha256-chain}.  Two clocks because two different things are kept -- the audit record says what the system DID, the conversation is personal data somebody may ask to have erased, and keeping the first while dropping the second is what satisfies Art. 19(1) and GDPR at once.  0 days = keep until deleted.  All three inherit most-restrictive-wins (LONGER for the two minimums), and 0 cannot win it.  Absent = delete removes everything, exactly as before -- this block changes what DELETE MEANS, so it has no default.
data.name: record_keeping

data.description: Garbage-collection strategy + thresholds for this session (type + threshold_percent / target / preserve_recent_turns). None = framework default.
data.name: gc

data.description: Session-scoped env vars (support ${VAR} expansion + secret URIs, e.g. vault://secret/app#key). Applied for the session's duration, never leak to other sessions.
data.name: env

data.description: Parent profile names to inherit from (tier-1 _base_* / profile-set composition). Resolved + flattened at discover_profiles(); cleared after.
data.name: inherits

data.description: JSON Schema constraining signal_completion's `payload` (inline dict or a path under .jaato/completion_schemas/). Carried on the tool so providers enforce it at sampling time + LifecycleTools validates server-side. None = legacy `summary: str`.
data.name: completion_payload_schema

data.description: JSON Schema constraining the spawn-time payload (input boundary), mirror of completion_payload_schema in everything but the type system. Inline dict or a .jaato/spawn_schemas/ path (spawn_schema_loader resolves it; the field previously named completion_schemas/ here, which is the OTHER schema's root). TYPE EVERY PROPERTY `string`: agent_params cross the IPC wire as `key=value` argv tokens, so the daemon validates strings and a property typed integer/number/boolean/object/array is refused on EVERY spawn (add a `pattern` for shape and parse in the prefetch). #883 ratified that as the contract, so BOTH boundaries — this one and the model-driven spawn_subagent call, where a model emitting `{"n": 1}` used to hand the validator a real int — validate the wire's string view, and a refusal caused by the schema says so. `jaato-scaffold validate` reports it before a spawn as spawn_schema_type_unreachable.
data.name: spawn_payload_schema

data.description: kb Python hooks (.jaato/scripts/processors/, probed for `render` and/or `validate`) run after jsonschema.validate passes; a validator's error list blocks completion, a renderer produces files. Inheritance concatenates parent + child; all fire. To drop ONE inherited processor, name it in `suppress_inherited_processors` — an empty list here adds nothing, it does not clear the parents'.
data.name: completion_processors

data.description: Names (or script paths) of INHERITED completion_processors this profile declines — the only way to scope down a key that otherwise only concatenates. Matches a parent entry's `name` or its `script`. An entry matching nothing is a load error. Not inherited further; only meaningful alongside `inherits`.
data.name: suppress_inherited_processors

data.description: Per-session resource caps (memory, PIDs, CPU weight, tool wall-clock timeout, stdout, max_parallel_tools). 'How much can it consume' — orthogonal to AppArmor's 'what can it touch'. None = host defaults.
data.name: runtime_limits

data.allowed: canonical tier keys: dispatcher, executor, planner, vision  |  or any name matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,31}$ (a 'description' is then required)  |  at most 8 tiers  |  reserved control keys: fallback, initial
data.description: Per-turn model-tier selection. Single-level dict mapping a tier key to a model (a model-name string, or {model (required), provider (optional; tiers may span providers), description (optional; prose the model reads as that tier's bullet in the enter_tier tool — default is the framework's own wording for the tier name), modalities (optional; non-text roles this tier fills per direction, e.g. {"image": "inbound"} or the inbound-sugar list ["image"]; directions are inbound / outbound / bidirectional — the content gate and the startup capability check resolve a tier BY ROLE, a tier named vision implies image inbound, and outbound roles parse but are inert until media delivery lands)}), plus the reserved control keys initial / fallback. Tier keys are the four canonical names (planner / dispatcher / executor / vision) or any name the deployment picks matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,31}$ — a deployment-named tier REQUIRES a description, and there is no JAATO_TIER_* env spelling for one. At most 8 tiers per session (each costs a bullet and an enum entry in the prompt-cache prefix, on every request). The enter_tier tool advertises ONLY the declared tiers. Non-empty silently ignores `model` (warns at load) — the active model is picked per turn from model_tiers[<active_tier>]. Empty = single-model mode (falls back to the JAATO_TIER_* env vars, then `model`).
data.name: model_tiers

data.allowed: limits dimensions: seconds, tokens, tool_calls, turns, usd  |  degrade[].at: percentage in (0, 100] (70 or '70%'; strictly increasing across rungs)  |  degrade[].model_tiers: overlay keyed by tier name  |  degrade[].action: abort, escalate, finalize, notify
data.description: Multi-dimensional budget ceilings + graceful degradation. `limits`: usd / tokens / seconds / tool_calls / turns (omit a dimension to leave it unbounded). `degrade`: an ordered ladder of rungs; a rung fires when ANY dimension crosses its `at` percentage and overlays new model_tiers bindings (a brownout — the tier vocabulary and the model's role are untouched, only the model each tier points at changes) and/or takes a terminal action (finalize / abort / escalate). Inheritance: limits MIN-WINS (a child may only tighten), degrade is scalar-override. None = unbudgeted.
data.name: budget_control

data.description: Opt into per-session kernel-enforced AppArmor confinement (best-effort; no-ops on hosts without AppArmor). False = unconfined. Resolution: create_headless_session kwarg > this field > legacy unconfined default.
data.name: apparmor

data.description: Opt the active provider into known wire-format / model-behavior workarounds (the provider reads the keys it knows; unknown keys warn). e.g. coerce_typed_tool_args (vllm).

data.allowed: 'default' (also when absent) = the framework set [*_API_KEY, *_APIKEY, *_TOKEN, *_SECRET, *_SECRET_KEY, *_PASSWORD, *_PASSWD, *_ACCESS_KEY, *_ACCESS_KEY_ID, *_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_CREDENTIALS, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN]  |  'none' = off, announced at WARNING  |  a list of globs; the entry 'default' expands in place and '!NAME' exempts a variable  |  applies to plugins: cli, interactive_shell, mcp
data.description: Secret env-var globs stripped from every model-driven subprocess (cli / interactive_shell / mcp). Absent = the framework set (*_API_KEY, *_TOKEN, *_SECRET, ...) — scrubbing is ON by default. `default` names that set; `none` opts out (announced at WARNING); a list of globs may carry `default` and `!NAME` exemption entries, e.g. [default, '!GH_TOKEN']. plugin_configs.<surface>.scrub_secret_env overrides this for one surface.
data.name: scrub_secret_env

data.description: Scope WHICH AppArmor .rules fragments compose this session's policy, by basename, from the fragment search path (~/.jaato/apparmor-fragments/, <workspace>/.jaato/apparmor-fragments/, + the .cache/ layer). None = compose ALL fragments; [] = none (maximally locked-down).

profile.text:
profile schema  (.jaato/profiles/<set>/<agent>.yaml fields):
  name                   str                         (required)
      Unique profile identifier (the <agent>.yaml stem).
  description            str                         (required)
      Human-readable summary of what this (sub)agent does.
  plugins                List[str]                 
      Plugin names to enable. `name(preload)` bypasses deferred tool-loading (all its tools, incl. discoverable, enter the initial context); `name(tools:[a,b])` scopes which tools are exposed (see tool_scopes).
  preloaded_plugins      set                       
      NOT a profile-file key — derived from plugins: — write `todo(preload)`.  DERIVED from `(preload)` annotations in `plugins` during parsing — not set directly.
  tool_scopes            Dict[str, List[str]]      
      NOT a profile-file key — derived from plugins: — write `memory(tools:[a,b])`.  Per-plugin tool allow-lists (plugin -> [tool names to expose]); every other tool that plugin ships is dropped from this session's wire + grammar. Absent plugin = all its tools. Keep in sync with the persona's referenced tools.
  plugin_configs         Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] 
      Per-plugin config overrides (plugin name -> config dict), e.g. plugin_configs.<provider>.api_params / .extra_body, plugin_configs.permission.policy.
  system_instructions    Optional[str]             
      DEPRECATED — use agents (.jaato/agents/<name>.md) instead; an `--agent`'s rendered markdown replaces this. Profiles should carry runtime config only.
  default_agent          Optional[str]             
      Agent definition (.jaato/agents/<name>.md) whose persona this profile spawns with when the caller names no `agent`. A profile supplies plugins, an agent supplies instructions — this binds the two so `spawn_subagent(profile=...)` alone yields a subagent that has both. An explicit `agent=` wins.
  suppress_base_instructions Any                         (default False)
      Drop framework-injected instruction layers from the system prompt (plugin + agent instructions always kept).  `true` drops the disk BASE layer (.jaato/instructions/*.md) AND the framework constants (task-completion, parallel guidance, turn-summary); the security untrusted-content boundary and the AI disclosure (EU AI Act Art. 50(1)) are kept.  A dict gives granular control over the four pieces, e.g. `{disk: true, constants: true, security: false}` (absent key = keep); dropping `security` or `disclosure` is a posture change and is announced at WARNING.  Saves ~3-5k tokens/turn for narrow goal-focused agents.  Default False.  Normalized to a canonical frozenset of piece names in __post_init__.
  model                  Optional[str]             
      Model override (uses the parent's model if unset). Silently ignored when model_tiers is non-empty.
  provider               Optional[str]             
      Provider override (e.g. anthropic, nebius, vllm). A profile binds exactly one provider + model.
  max_completion_nudges  Optional[int]             
      How many times the framework re-prompts a session that ended without calling signal_completion before giving up (NudgeExhausted). Per turn. None = the framework default, 2. Raise it for a model that reliably does the work and unreliably reports it done (audio models routinely burn a nudge on a redundant enter_tier). Positive integer; the sibling of a processor's max_refusals.
  cache                  Optional[ForwardRef('CacheProfileConfig')]
      Prompt-cache defaults, cross-provider. {enabled: auto|true|false, ttl: 5m|1h, history: bool}. 'auto' leaves the provider's own default alone and is a no-op on a provider that cannot cache. plugin_configs.<provider> overrides this for mechanism-specific tuning (more specific wins).
  trace                  Optional[ForwardRef('TraceProfileConfig')]
      Diagnostic trace-log paths: {session_log, provider_log, ledger}. Typed sibling of the JAATO_TRACE_LOG / JAATO_PROVIDER_TRACE / LEDGER_PATH env vars, which stay the lower-precedence default (this block outranks them). Absolute = one shared file; relative = one file per session, resolved against the workspace. Refuses a switch written into a path field -- `env: {JAATO_PROVIDER_TRACE: '1'}` is a valid str and wrote every session's trace to a file named `1` (#775).
  regulatory             Optional[ForwardRef('RegulatoryProfileConfig')]
      allowed → risk_class: minimal | limited | high (most-restrictive-wins across inherits)  |  keys: annex_iii, disclosure_text, intended_purpose, interacts_with_persons, provider, risk_class  |  provider: {name, contact}  |  absent = undeclared
      What this application declares about itself under the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689): {intended_purpose, risk_class: minimal|limited|high, annex_iii, provider: {name, contact}, interacts_with_persons, disclosure_text}.  Declared, never inferred -- whether a use is high-risk is the provider's own determination (Art. 6(4)).  `validate` escalates its warnings to errors under risk_class: high; the disclosure piece reads provider.name and interacts_with_persons (Art. 50(1)).  risk_class inherits most-restrictive-wins, the other fields child-replaces.  Absent = undeclared (validated as minimal, documented as unknown).
  record_keeping         Optional[ForwardRef('RecordKeepingConfig')]
      How long this session's records are kept and whether they carry tamper evidence (EU AI Act Arts. 12, 19, 26(6)): {retention_days, conversation_retention_days, integrity: none|sha256-chain}.  Two clocks because two different things are kept -- the audit record says what the system DID, the conversation is personal data somebody may ask to have erased, and keeping the first while dropping the second is what satisfies Art. 19(1) and GDPR at once.  0 days = keep until deleted.  All three inherit most-restrictive-wins (LONGER for the two minimums), and 0 cannot win it.  Absent = delete removes everything, exactly as before -- this block changes what DELETE MEANS, so it has no default.
  gc                     Optional[GCProfileConfig] 
      Garbage-collection strategy + thresholds for this session (type + threshold_percent / target / preserve_recent_turns). None = framework default.
  env                    Dict[str, str]            
      Session-scoped env vars (support ${VAR} expansion + secret URIs, e.g. vault://secret/app#key). Applied for the session's duration, never leak to other sessions.
  inherits               Optional[List[str]]       
      Parent profile names to inherit from (tier-1 _base_* / profile-set composition). Resolved + flattened at discover_profiles(); cleared after.
  completion_payload_schema Union[str, Dict[str, Any], None]
      JSON Schema constraining signal_completion's `payload` (inline dict or a path under .jaato/completion_schemas/). Carried on the tool so providers enforce it at sampling time + LifecycleTools validates server-side. None = legacy `summary: str`.
  spawn_payload_schema   Union[str, Dict[str, Any], None]
      JSON Schema constraining the spawn-time payload (input boundary), mirror of completion_payload_schema in everything but the type system. Inline dict or a .jaato/spawn_schemas/ path (spawn_schema_loader resolves it; the field previously named completion_schemas/ here, which is the OTHER schema's root). TYPE EVERY PROPERTY `string`: agent_params cross the IPC wire as `key=value` argv tokens, so the daemon validates strings and a property typed integer/number/boolean/object/array is refused on EVERY spawn (add a `pattern` for shape and parse in the prefetch). #883 ratified that as the contract, so BOTH boundaries — this one and the model-driven spawn_subagent call, where a model emitting `{"n": 1}` used to hand the validator a real int — validate the wire's string view, and a refusal caused by the schema says so. `jaato-scaffold validate` reports it before a spawn as spawn_schema_type_unreachable.
  completion_processors  List[CompletionProcessor] 
      kb Python hooks (.jaato/scripts/processors/, probed for `render` and/or `validate`) run after jsonschema.validate passes; a validator's error list blocks completion, a renderer produces files. Inheritance concatenates parent + child; all fire. To drop ONE inherited processor, name it in `suppress_inherited_processors` — an empty list here adds nothing, it does not clear the parents'.
  suppress_inherited_processors List[str]                 
      Names (or script paths) of INHERITED completion_processors this profile declines — the only way to scope down a key that otherwise only concatenates. Matches a parent entry's `name` or its `script`. An entry matching nothing is a load error. Not inherited further; only meaningful alongside `inherits`.
  runtime_limits         Optional[RuntimeLimits]   
      Per-session resource caps (memory, PIDs, CPU weight, tool wall-clock timeout, stdout, max_parallel_tools). 'How much can it consume' — orthogonal to AppArmor's 'what can it touch'. None = host defaults.
  model_tiers            Dict[str, Any]            
      allowed → canonical tier keys: dispatcher, executor, planner, vision  |  or any name matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,31}$ (a 'description' is then required)  |  at most 8 tiers  |  reserved control keys: fallback, initial
      Per-turn model-tier selection. Single-level dict mapping a tier key to a model (a model-name string, or {model (required), provider (optional; tiers may span providers), description (optional; prose the model reads as that tier's bullet in the enter_tier tool — default is the framework's own wording for the tier name), modalities (optional; non-text roles this tier fills per direction, e.g. {"image": "inbound"} or the inbound-sugar list ["image"]; directions are inbound / outbound / bidirectional — the content gate and the startup capability check resolve a tier BY ROLE, a tier named vision implies image inbound, and outbound roles parse but are inert until media delivery lands)}), plus the reserved control keys initial / fallback. Tier keys are the four canonical names (planner / dispatcher / executor / vision) or any name the deployment picks matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,31}$ — a deployment-named tier REQUIRES a description, and there is no JAATO_TIER_* env spelling for one. At most 8 tiers per session (each costs a bullet and an enum entry in the prompt-cache prefix, on every request). The enter_tier tool advertises ONLY the declared tiers. Non-empty silently ignores `model` (warns at load) — the active model is picked per turn from model_tiers[<active_tier>]. Empty = single-model mode (falls back to the JAATO_TIER_* env vars, then `model`).
  budget_control         Optional[BudgetControlConfig]
      allowed → limits dimensions: seconds, tokens, tool_calls, turns, usd  |  degrade[].at: percentage in (0, 100] (70 or '70%'; strictly increasing across rungs)  |  degrade[].model_tiers: overlay keyed by tier name  |  degrade[].action: abort, escalate, finalize, notify
      Multi-dimensional budget ceilings + graceful degradation. `limits`: usd / tokens / seconds / tool_calls / turns (omit a dimension to leave it unbounded). `degrade`: an ordered ladder of rungs; a rung fires when ANY dimension crosses its `at` percentage and overlays new model_tiers bindings (a brownout — the tier vocabulary and the model's role are untouched, only the model each tier points at changes) and/or takes a terminal action (finalize / abort / escalate). Inheritance: limits MIN-WINS (a child may only tighten), degrade is scalar-override. None = unbudgeted.
  apparmor               bool                        (default False)
      Opt into per-session kernel-enforced AppArmor confinement (best-effort; no-ops on hosts without AppArmor). False = unconfined. Resolution: create_headless_session kwarg > this field > legacy unconfined default.
  quirks                 Dict[str, Any]            
      Opt the active provider into known wire-format / model-behavior workarounds (the provider reads the keys it knows; unknown keys warn). e.g. coerce_typed_tool_args (vllm).
  scrub_secret_env       Optional[Any]             
      allowed → 'default' (also when absent) = the framework set [*_API_KEY, *_APIKEY, *_TOKEN, *_SECRET, *_SECRET_KEY, *_PASSWORD, *_PASSWD, *_ACCESS_KEY, *_ACCESS_KEY_ID, *_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_CREDENTIALS, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN]  |  'none' = off, announced at WARNING  |  a list of globs; the entry 'default' expands in place and '!NAME' exempts a variable  |  applies to plugins: cli, interactive_shell, mcp
      Secret env-var globs stripped from every model-driven subprocess (cli / interactive_shell / mcp). Absent = the framework set (*_API_KEY, *_TOKEN, *_SECRET, ...) — scrubbing is ON by default. `default` names that set; `none` opts out (announced at WARNING); a list of globs may carry `default` and `!NAME` exemption entries, e.g. [default, '!GH_TOKEN']. plugin_configs.<surface>.scrub_secret_env overrides this for one surface.
  apparmor_fragments     Optional[List[str]]       
      Scope WHICH AppArmor .rules fragments compose this session's policy, by basename, from the fragment search path (~/.jaato/apparmor-fragments/, <workspace>/.jaato/apparmor-fragments/, + the .cache/ layer). None = compose ALL fragments; [] = none (maximally locked-down).
  apparmor_fragments_source Optional[str]             
      NOT a profile-file key — derived from which profile in the inherits: chain declared `apparmor_fragments`.  The profile that declared apparmor_fragments, resolved through inherits:. Derived, not settable.

  trace: — the two diagnostic log paths plus the token LEDGER, the ONE
  knob whose value is a path the framework writes to.  All three keys
  take the same rules:
    absolute   one file, shared by every session using this profile
    relative   resolved against each session's own workspace by the
               READER (jaato_sdk/trace.py) — one file per session
    refused    a switch (1 / true / off), a directory, an unknown
               {token} — each fails at profile LOAD, by name

        trace:
          provider_log: .jaato/logs/provider{agent_suffix}.jsonl
          session_log:  .jaato/logs/session.jsonl
          ledger:       .jaato/logs/ledger.jsonl   # every round trip +
                                                  # permission verdict

  A PROVIDER trace splits per agent whether or not you ask: with no
  placeholder the agent id is appended before the extension
  (provider.jsonl -> provider_subagent_1.jsonl).  Naming a placeholder
  puts it where you want it instead, and is the only way to split a
  SESSION trace, which never splits on its own.

  SUBSTITUTION — what a value may contain, and when it is resolved:

    resolved by expand_variables (daemon, at profile resolution):
      ${cwd}             the session's workspace root, else the resolving process's cwd
      ${workspaceRoot}   the workspace root detected from .git / .jaato
      ${jdtlsStateRoot}  the framework-managed jdtls state directory, a sibling of the workspace (Eclipse forbids it inside the project)
      ${HOME}            the resolving process's $HOME
      ${USER}            the resolving process's $USER
      ${ANY_ENV_VAR}     any process / session env var; an UNDEFINED name is left literal, and a literal ${...} in a path is created as a directory
      → honoured in: env:, plugin_configs:, trace:, and plugin configs that expand (lsp, webhook, web_fetch, service_connector, references)

    resolved by jaato_sdk.trace (the writer, per line):
      {agent}         the agent writing the line -- `main` for the main agent, `subagent_1`, `subagent_2`, ... for spawned subagents
      {agent_suffix}  `_subagent_1` for a subagent and EMPTY for the main agent -- what the implicit form appends, placeable anywhere in the path
      → honoured in: trace.session_log / trace.provider_log / trace.ledger and their env vars

    The two vocabularies are told apart by the `$`, and do NOT overlap:
    `${agent}` is an env var nobody sets; `{agent}` is the per-agent token.
    A `{token}` the framework does not know is REFUSED in `trace:` at profile
    load and reported by `validate` — unresolved, it becomes a literal directory.

  AppArmor — add client-side extra rules via the profile:
    apparmor: true              opt the session into kernel-enforced confinement
    apparmor_fragments:         compose only these .rules fragments (by basename), from the
      - my_extra_rules          search path ~/.jaato/apparmor-fragments/ and
                                <workspace>/.jaato/apparmor-fragments/ (+ the .cache/ layer).
    drop <name>.rules in that dir, then list <name>.  null = ALL fragments; [] = none.

  inheritance (`inherits: [_base_<stage>]`) — how a child profile merges with its
  parent(s), resolved at discover_profiles() (config.py:_merge_profiles):
    plugins                      UNION / additive — child ADDS to the parents'; it
                                 CANNOT scope DOWN here (the list only grows). `[]`
                                 in the child ADDS NOTHING — it does NOT clear the
                                 parents'. There is NO spelling that clears them.
                                 To reduce the surface, re-list the plugin carrying
                                 an allow-list — `plugins: [memory(tools:[a,b])]` —
                                 or use the permission whitelist, or do not inherit.
    preloaded_plugins,           DERIVED, never written: both come out of the
    tool_scopes                  `plugins` entries' own modifiers, so a top-level
                                 `preloaded_plugins:` / `tool_scopes:` in a profile
                                 FILE is read by NOBODY (`validate` reports it as
                                 `derived_profile_key`).  Write them as
                                 `plugins: [todo(preload), memory(tools:[a,b])]`.
                                 They merge the way their source does —
                                 preloaded_plugins by UNION, tool_scopes per-KEY
                                 with the VALUE at a key REPLACED.  NB a child that
                                 re-lists a plugin with NO `tools:` modifier keeps
                                 the PARENT's allow-list; to widen it back the child
                                 must enumerate the wider set explicitly.
    completion_processors        CONCATENATED parent → child; all of them fire. `[]`
                                 in the child ADDS NOTHING — it does NOT clear the
                                 parents'. Scope DOWN by naming inherited entries in
                                 `suppress_inherited_processors` (matches an entry's
                                 `name`, else its `script`); an entry matching nothing
                                 is a load ERROR, and it is not inherited further.
    env, quirks                  per-KEY dict-merge — child wins on keys it sets;
                                 the parent's other keys survive.  The VALUE at a
                                 key is REPLACED, never merged into.
    plugin_configs               the same, one level deeper: merged per PLUGIN and
                                 then per KEY within it, so a sibling key survives
                                 — but the value at a key is still REPLACED.  A
                                 NESTED dict is NOT merged recursively:
                                   parent  openrouter.api_params {temperature: 0.0}
                                   child   openrouter.api_params {thinking: high}
                                   result  openrouter.api_params {thinking: high}
                                 `temperature` is GONE, nothing fails, and the two
                                 stages that override api_params are exactly the
                                 ones that lose the determinism the base hoisted.
                                 Repeat the shared keys in each child that sets any.
    model, provider, gc, cache,  child REPLACES — the child's value wins outright
    model_tiers, runtime_limits, (this is how a child scopes DOWN, unlike plugins).
    scrub_secret_env, default_agent,
    apparmor_fragments,          For the two payload schemas an empty dict `{}` IS a
    completion_payload_schema,   value and overrides; `null`/absent reads as unset and
    spawn_payload_schema         inherits.
    budget_control.limits,       MOST RESTRICTIVE wins — a child may only TIGHTEN a
    runtime_limits.              ceiling, never raise the one it was spawned under.
      max_parallel_tools         (budget_control.degrade is child-REPLACES, and so are
                                 runtime_limits' other, kernel-enforced ceilings.)
    suppress_base_instructions,  UNION / OR — STICKY: a piece any layer drops stays
    apparmor                     dropped, and a confined parent can't be un-confined.

  empty vs listed `plugins` (a REQUIRED key — authors must pick).  WITH NO PARENT
  (no `inherits:`) — this is the ONLY context in which [] means 'none':
    plugins: []   → tools=[] → NONE of the registry tool plugins; only the framework
                   set (permission, reliability, lifecycle/signal_completion) is wired.
                   (Pre-2026-06-07 a falsy bug made [] silently load ALL ~30 tools.)
    plugins: [x]  → exactly those.

  IN A CHILD (`inherits:` set) — [] does NOT mean 'none'.  The list is a UNION, so:
    plugins: []   → the parents' plugins, UNCHANGED.  Writing [] to lock a stage down
                   hands it the parent's ENTIRE tool surface, silently, with a profile
                   that validates cleanly.  Measured: parent [memory, todo] + child []
                   → [memory, todo].
    plugins: [x]  → the parents' plugins PLUS x.
    To scope DOWN per stage, re-list the plugin CARRYING an allow-list —
    `plugins: [memory(tools:[a,b])]`, which is the only spelling of tool_scopes — or
    use the permission plugin's whitelist, or do not inherit.  A bare name in the
    plugins list only ADDS to the inherited set.
    NB `[]` is not one vocabulary across this schema: for apparmor_fragments above it
    DOES mean none.  Read each key's own row; do not generalise from a neighbour.

  declining ONE inherited completion_processor (the only removal opt-out there is):
    inherits: [_base_worker]
    suppress_inherited_processors:
      - acceptance              a parent entry's `name:`, or its `script:` path
    Everything else scopes down by REPLACING a value, never by removing an entry.
    Don't stop inheriting just to drop a processor: you lose budget_control,
    runtime_limits, env and plugin_configs with it, silently.

provider anthropic.text:
provider: anthropic
  capabilities: user_message_images, tool_result_images, pdf_input, thinking, prompt_caching, streaming, cancellation
  quirks: (none)
  resolution order:
    credentials    : api_key_param:api_key → oauth:anthropic_oauth.json → env:ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN → env:CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN → env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY   (first source that yields a credential wins)
    context window : catalog/endpoint detect → profile knob 'context_length' → else error  (detect WINS over the knob)
    modalities     : catalog detect → profile knob 'modalities' → static table → text floor
    layered knobs  : layer dict → flat key (deprecated, warns) → default
  knobs (plugin_configs.anthropic.*):
    [top_level]  — auth / identity + prompt-cache control
      api_key                str     Anthropic API key (sk-ant-api...)
      oauth_token            str     OAuth token for Pro/Max subscription
      enable_caching         bool    cache_control breakpoints on system/tools/history; unset resolves JAATO_ANTHROPIC_ENABLE_CACHING (default off)
      cache_ttl              str     5m | 1h (1h costs a 2x write premium)  (default '5m')
      cache_history          bool    place the history breakpoint (BP3), not just system+tools  (default True)
      cache_exclude_recent_turns int     BP3 fallback turn count when no InstructionBudget is set  (default 2)
      cache_min_tokens       bool    enforce Anthropic's minimum cacheable size before spending a breakpoint  (default True)
    [api_params]  — Anthropic Messages API request-body fields
      temperature            float 
      top_p                  float 
      top_k                  int   
      max_tokens             int   
      enable_thinking        bool  
      thinking_budget        int   
    [framework_overrides]  — rare escape hatches
      context_length         int   
      modalities             list  
  api_params — scope of the check:
    `validate` checks these against THIS PROVIDER's allow-list, not against
    the model you named: a key can be a valid provider knob and still be a
    400 on one model (reasoning models commonly accept only the DEFAULT
    temperature / top_p, and reject an explicit 0.0).  Which values a model
    takes is the vendor's documentation, not a fact this framework holds.
    OMITTING a parameter is always safe — it is never the cause of a 400.

auth.name: DefaultAzureCredential

modalities.description: OUTPUT selector ["text","audio"] — OpenAI's field, the opposite direction from the tier key of the same name

api_version.description: REQUIRED — the api-version date, e.g. 2024-10-21; no default, because it decides which request fields exist

auth.description: "key" (resource key) or "aad" (Microsoft Entra ID, needs the azure-identity package)

context_length.description: REQUIRED — Azure reports no per-deployment window, and a deployment name does not identify the model behind it

extra_body.description: opaque passthrough to OpenAI create() extra_body

model_name.description: the MODEL id this deployment serves, e.g. gpt-4o; the only thing that makes the input-modality table applicable, since the deployment name is arbitrary

output_modalities.description: assert what the model can EMIT; no catalog reports output modalities, so without this the floor is text and the startup check refuses an outbound tier role

notes: `model:` in a profile is the DEPLOYMENT name from your Azure resource (Azure AI Foundry -> Deployments), NOT a catalog model id. A catalog id that happens to be spelled like one fails at request time with DeploymentNotFound, and nothing earlier says why.
`plugin_configs.azure_openai.model_name` carries the model the deployment actually serves (e.g. gpt-4o). It is what makes the input-modality table applicable — a deployment name identifies nothing.
`api_version` is required and has no default: the date decides which request fields exist, so the framework must not pick one for you.

enable_thinking.description: request extended reasoning.  WARNS at connect: reasoning is extracted but not replayed, so a thinking turn that also calls tools may be rejected

max_tokens.description: output cap; always sent, because Converse has no server-side default worth relying on across seven vendors

region.description: AWS region, e.g. us-east-1.  Bedrock is regional and model availability differs by region, so there is no default.  Unset falls through to JAATO_BEDROCK_REGION, then AWS_REGION (read here because Python's botocore does not), then boto3's own AWS_DEFAULT_REGION / profile region
