runtime.text:
jaato runtime — entities, workspace flow, logs, how to debug
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
ENTITIES
  daemon   long-lived singleton on the IPC socket; daemon-tier plugins,
           provider / OAuth / GC / sessions live here.
  session  per-conversation state (history/profile/workspace):
           session.new -> bootstrap -> runner spawn -> plugin init -> turns.
  runner   per-session SUBPROCESS running the model loop + RUNNER-TIER
           plugins (filesystem_query/file_edit/cli/lsp/mcp/notebook);
           pool-served (warm) or cold-spawned; its OWN ContextVars + env.

WORKSPACE FLOW  (the path-tool 'workspace=none' class of bug)
  client   IPCClient(workspace_path=ws) -> set_workspace + working_dir
  daemon   working_dir -> session.workspace_path -> envelope.workspace_path
  runner   envelope.workspace_path -> registry.set_workspace_path (config+hook)
           + set_workspace_root() ContextVar + os.environ, BEFORE expose_all
  plugin   initialize() reads config['workspace_root'] / get_workspace_root()
           -> caches self._workspace_root (path tools enforce this boundary)
  BREAKS   working_dir not sent, OR runner didn't seed the ContextVar/env
           -> workspace=none -> path tools Permission-denied (the #344 class)

LOGS  (under <workspace>/.jaato/)
  logs/runner-<sid>.log           runner bootstrap + runner-tier plugin init
                                  (where 'workspace=none' surfaces)
  logs/session_<id>_client_*.log  session-level
  sessions/<id>.json              history + workspace_path
  <daemon stdout/log>             daemon-tier (e.g. /tmp/jaato.log)

DEBUG A SESSION (one command — reads the logs above):
  jaato-doctor --session <id|latest> --workspace DIR
  -> reports whether the runner-tier path plugins resolved the workspace
     (PASS=<ws>) or got workspace=none (FAIL + the fix), plus the log map.

RUNTIME LIMITS  (profile `runtime_limits:` — what a session may CONSUME)
  field                 enforced by  effective when unset
  memory_max_mb         kernel       host default (no limit)
                                     cgroup v2 memory.max — OOM-kills the slice
  pids_max              kernel       host default (no limit)
                                     cgroup v2 pids.max — bounds fork/thread count
  cpu_weight            kernel       host default (no limit)
                                     cgroup v2 cpu.weight — fair-share, 1..10000
  tool_timeout_seconds  cli/shell    host default (no limit)
                                     subprocess.run(timeout=) per tool call
  max_output_bytes      cli/shell    host default (no limit)
                                     truncates captured stdout/stderr
  max_parallel_tools    session      8 (framework default)
                                     width of the tool thread pool (and of the token-count fan-out)
  max_session_seconds   daemon       unbounded
                                     total wall-clock a session may stay LOADED; 0 = unbounded
  max_orphan_seconds    daemon       900s (framework default)
                                     wall-clock with NO client attached before the daemon stops it; 0 = unbounded
  unload_grace_seconds  daemon       60s (framework default)
                                     wall-clock the daemon holds an unwatched session in memory before UNLOADING it (a reconnect inside it costs nothing); 0 = no grace
  seccomp               kernel (seccomp) default while a kernel boundary is active; no filter when unconfined
                                     syscall deny-list in every cli / shell / notebook subprocess: default | off (off is announced at WARNING)
  seccomp_allow         kernel (seccomp) none (every family denied)
                                     deny-list families allowed back for this stage, e.g. [ptrace]
  capabilities          kernel (capabilities) none while a kernel boundary is active (bounding, permitted, effective, inheritable and ambient empty); untouched when unconfined
                                     capabilities a cli / shell / notebook subprocess keeps: none | [names] | inherit (inherit is announced at WARNING)
  agent_params.isolated=true fills any field the profile omits: memory_max_mb=2048, pids_max=128, cpu_weight=100, tool_timeout_seconds=120.0, max_output_bytes=1048576
  inheritance: the ceilings are child-REPLACES (parents must agree);
               max_parallel_tools and the three daemon-layer fields
               are MIN across every layer that sets one, so a child
               may only ever narrow what it was spawned under.
  seccomp is MOST-RESTRICTIVE-WINS too: 'default' beats 'off', and
  seccomp_allow is the intersection of every declared list (#1503).
  capabilities likewise: 'none' beats a list beats 'inherit', and
  two lists keep only what both keep (#1543).
  seccomp families (each answers EPERM unless allowed back):
    kernel       module loading, kexec, reboot, swap, process accounting, syslog
    mount        the mount API, old and new
    namespaces   setns; unshare/clone with a CLONE_NEW* flag; clone3 answers ENOSYS so libc falls back to clone
    bpf          the bpf(2) syscall
    perf         perf events
    userfaultfd  userfaultfd
    io_uring     io_uring (runtimes fall back on EPERM)
    keyring      the kernel keyring
    fanotify     fanotify
    ptrace       debugging and cross-process memory access
    handles      file-handle tricks and uselib
    personality  personality(2) other than the default persona
  the 'daemon' layer is enforced by the SessionManager watchdog, not
  inside the session -- so it still applies when the client that created
  the session has died (#812).  max_orphan_seconds and
  unload_grace_seconds are the two fields here with a framework
  default: the session each exists for is the one whose profile
  declared nothing.  Declare 0 to opt out of either.
  unload_grace_seconds is the daemon layer's third field and the odd
  one out in its VERB: the two bounds STOP a session that ran too
  long, this one DELAYS the teardown of one that is merely unwatched,
  so a browser reload or a network blip no longer costs a full save +
  respawn (#1106).  It carries a framework default for the same reason
  max_orphan_seconds does, and 0 means NO grace (the pre-#1106
  behaviour) rather than 'unbounded' -- so a child declaring 0 wins
  the MIN, where a child declaring 0 for a bound does not.

data.cross_provider: V2 (#354): tiers may declare DIFFERENT providers; switch_tier swaps to a cached per-tier provider instance (history is provider-neutral; switch-back is O(1)). e.g. a cheap zhipuai text executor + a gemini/OpenRouter vision tier in ONE profile.
data.description: each tier entry may carry a 'description' — prose the MODEL reads as that tier's bullet in the enter_tier tool schema (default: the framework's own wording for the name).  the enter_tier enum lists only the tiers the profile DECLARES, so an undeclared tier is never advertised.  read once when the tool schema is built (it sits in the prompt-cache prefix), so a budget degrade rung cannot set it.
data.free_tier_names: a profile may declare tiers under names of its OWN — 'coder', 'reviewer', 'researcher' — matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,31}$ (lowercase, digits, underscores, starting with a letter, 2-32 chars).  a free name MUST carry a 'description': the four canonical names come with framework prose, a name the framework has never heard of does not, and 'routes this session to <model>' is not a reason for the model to enter a tier.  free names sort after the canonical ones in the enter_tier schema, so adding one never reorders the prompt-cache prefix ahead of them.
data.inbound_gate_fallback: no tier config, no active tier, a tier not in the config, or an active tier that declared NO role of its own -> the model's catalog capability ALONE decides, exactly as before #1001.  a tier named 'vision' carrying only its IMPLICIT {image: inbound} does NOT arm the gate either: that implication exists so profiles written before the modalities key are unchanged, and arming off it would make the shim CHANGE their behaviour.  write any role on that tier and it arms — and then still admits image, which is part of its set, just not the trigger.
data.inbound_gate_is_armed_by_any_role: a tier that declares ANY role — in EITHER direction — is handed, out of the whole vocabulary (audio, file, image, video), ONLY the kinds it declared inbound.  so declaring {audio: outbound} is HOW YOU STOP inbound audio reaching a tier that only speaks: a tier declared to speak is read as a decision about what it RECEIVES too.  the trigger is 'did the author write a role', NOT 'is the inbound set non-empty' — an outbound-only tier arms the gate with an EMPTY inbound set, which is the whole point.  it NARROWS, never widens: the tier's set is INTERSECTED with what the model's catalog accepts, so declaring a role a model cannot take still withholds (most-restrictive-wins, as runtime_limits.max_parallel_tools).  #1001.
data.inbound_is_inert_when_unmarshalled: an INBOUND role is INERT in the same way when the provider does not declare the capability that carries it (image -> user_message_images, file -> pdf_input, audio -> audio_input): the model may well accept the content, but the converter withholds it with a note.  that asymmetry — a catalog saying `audio` and a converter with no branch for it — was #830.  a kind with no capability column (video) is left unchecked rather than declared inert.
data.modalities_key: a tier declares which non-text modalities it fills (audio, file, image, video) and in which direction (bidirectional, inbound, outbound).  list form [image] is sugar for inbound.  the content gate and the startup capability check resolve the tier BY ROLE, not by the name 'vision' — which still implies image inbound so pre-existing profiles are unchanged.  this DECLARES a role and is VERIFIED (a tier whose model can't accept the modality fails loud at connect); the opposite of plugin_configs.<provider>.modalities, which ASSERTS capability to correct catalog detection.
data.outbound_is_inert: the EMISSION half of an OUTBOUND role is INERT unless the named provider declares `output_media` — the adapters that decode model-generated media off the stream (openrouter + the _openai_compat five today).  validate warns only when it does not, so a working speaking tier is not told it does nothing.  the role itself is NOT inert: writing any role ARMS the inbound gate for that tier (see inbound_gate_is_armed_by_any_role), so {audio: outbound} is live whatever the provider can emit.  see docs/design/binary-media-chunks.md.
data.shape: model_tiers: { <tier>: <model-str> | {model, provider, description, modalities}, initial: <tier>, fallback: <tier> }
data.switching: the MODEL calls enter_tier('<tier>') mid-session; the active tier selects the model (and, V2, the provider); history is preserved across the switch
data.vision: 'vision' is the ONE tier name with a built-in meaning: it implies modalities {image: inbound}, so profiles written before the modalities key are unchanged.  Nothing else is name-based — the gate and the startup check resolve a tier BY ROLE, so an image tier may be called anything as long as it declares the role.  content the ACTIVE model cannot accept trips the content gate: a synthetic 'enter_tier("<tier>") first' naming whichever tier declares the role, which the agent self-corrects on.  user-message images ride the attachment ferry (#353): SDK send_message(attachments=[path | {mime_type,data,display_name}])
data.why_the_tier_and_not_the_format: the framework cannot know which CONTAINERS a model accepts.  openai/gpt-audio lists audio input in the catalog and takes only wav/mp3, so supports_modality('audio') is true and useless — a jaato-side format allowlist could only ever be stale in one of two directions (withholding what a model accepts, or passing what it rejects), the argument api_params already makes about per-model tables.  what the tier declared IS knowable, and is written by you — which is why this is gated by role and not by format.

tiers.text:
jaato model tiers — multi-model sessions (cognitive + modality roles) ---------------------------------------------------------------- CANONICAL dispatcher, executor, planner, vision (the names the FRAMEWORK has prose for; 'vision' also implies modalities {image: inbound}) YOUR OWN any name matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,31}$ -- 'coder', 'reviewer', 'researcher'. a free name REQUIRES a 'description' (the framework has none for it) and has no JAATO_TIER_* env spelling. at most 8 tiers per session -- each one is a bullet + an enum entry in the prompt-cache prefix, paid on EVERY request. CONTROL KEYS fallback, initial (reserved: initial tier + fallback) SHAPE (in a profile) model_tiers: : OR {model: , provider:

, description: , modalities: {: }} initial: # the tier a session starts in fallback: # when enter_tier names an undeclared tier EXIT (what ends a tier's turn at the wheel) exit_on: switch (default) stays until something switches it exit_on: completion entered, does ONE completion, left again -- the framework returns to the calling tier and reports what the delegate produced, so the model in the specialist tier does NOTHING to hand back. use it when that model is the one least able to: a speaking tier measured over four runs never returned on its own. SWITCHING the MODEL calls enter_tier('') mid-session; the active tier picks the model (and, V2, the provider). conversation history is preserved. DESCRIPTION (what the model reads) the enter_tier tool advertises ONLY the tiers this profile declares, each with a bullet. the bullet is the tier's 'description' when set, else the framework's own wording for that name — so a ladder whose 'executor' means something specific to your deployment can say so, and a ladder that would rather call it 'coder' can do THAT instead (a deployment-named tier must carry the description). it is read once, when the tool schema is built: the tool block sits in the prompt-cache prefix, so a budget degrade rung may NOT set one. MODALITY ROLES (which tier can SEE what) a tier may declare modalities: {: } where kind is one of audio, file, image, video and direction is one of bidirectional, inbound, outbound. the list form modalities: [image] is sugar for inbound. content of a modality the ACTIVE model can't accept is withheld by the content gate, which names a tier that declares the role: a synthetic 'enter_tier("") first' the agent self-corrects on. the tier is found BY ROLE, so an image tier need not be called 'vision' — though that name still implies ['image'], so older profiles are unchanged. a tier whose model cannot accept a role it declares fails LOUD at connect, not at the first image. NOTE this DECLARES a role and is VERIFIED — the opposite direction from plugin_configs..modalities, which ASSERTS what a model supports to correct catalog detection. OUTBOUND roles are DELIVERED by any provider declaring `output_media` (openrouter + the _openai_compat five today); `validate` warns only when the named provider does not. that warning is about EMISSION only — the role is never inert, because declaring it also bounds what the tier RECEIVES (below). see docs/design/binary-media-chunks.md. INBOUND roles are MARSHALLED by any provider declaring the matching capability (image -> user_message_images, file -> pdf_input, audio -> audio_input); `validate` warns when the named provider does not, since the model may accept content its own converter then withholds (#830). user-message images ride the attachment ferry — SDK send_message(attachments=...). WHAT A TIER IS HANDED (declaring a role bounds it -- #1001) a tier that declares ANY role, in EITHER direction, receives only the kinds it declared INBOUND. the counter-intuitive consequence is the useful one: voz: {model: openai/gpt-audio, modalities: {audio: outbound}} is HOW YOU STOP the caller's recorded audio reaching a tier that only SPEAKS. your decision that a tier speaks is honoured as a decision about what it is given. ARMED BY 'did the author write a role', NOT 'is the inbound set non-empty' -- an outbound-only tier arms it with an EMPTY inbound set, which is the case above. NOT ARMED no tier config; no active tier; a tier absent from the config; a tier that declared no role of its own; or a tier named 'vision' carrying ONLY its implied [image] (that implication exists so pre-modalities profiles are unchanged, so arming off it would defeat its purpose). in every one of those the MODEL's catalog decides alone, exactly as before. NARROWS the tier's set is INTERSECTED with the model's catalog, so declaring a role the model cannot take still withholds. a declaration never grants (most-restrictive-wins, as runtime_limits.max_parallel_tools). WHY HERE the framework cannot know which CONTAINERS a model accepts: openai/gpt-audio lists audio input and takes only wav/mp3, so supports_modality('audio') is true and useless. what YOU declared is knowable -- which is why this is gated by role, and not by a format allowlist that could only be stale in one of two directions. withheld content leaves a note naming the TIER (not the model, which may read the kind perfectly well) and a tier that declares the role. CROSS-PROVIDER (V2) tiers may declare DIFFERENT providers — switch_tier swaps to a cached per-tier provider instance (history is provider-neutral; switch-back is O(1)). e.g. a cheap zhipuai text executor + a gemini/OpenRouter vision tier in ONE profile (no need to relocate the whole profile).

in_process.scope: embedded — no daemon, no socket; the agent runs in your process

ipc.auth: none — any principal that can open the socket drives the agent

websocket.sdk: jaato-sdk (Python) — jaato_sdk.WSClient / jaato.session(mode='ws'); also jaato-sdk-ts (TypeScript) / browser client jaato-web-coder-ui

transports.text:
client transports — one facade (jaato.session(mode=...)), three modes
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  in_process            IPC (Unix socket)        WebSocket
  - embedded, no daemon - local daemon           - remote daemon / browser
  - InProcessClient     - IPCClient              - WSClient (Python)
                                                   + TS SDK / jaato-web-coder-ui
  - n/a (no wire)       - unauthenticated        - bearer-token authenticated
                          (socket-mode 660)

  Python ships a client for ALL THREE; the SAME Session.ask/.complete/
  .stream facade rides on each.  mode is the only variable.

daemon flags (ipc / ws only — in_process needs no daemon):
  IPC:  --ipc-socket PATH   [--socket-mode 660]
  WS:   --web-socket [HOST:]PORT
        --ws-token TOKEN | --ws-token-file PATH | --ws-unsafe-no-auth
        (no token flag → daemon auto-generates ~/.jaato/ws.token, 0600)

WS auth contract — a client presents ONE of:
  Authorization: Bearer <token>   (header — SDK / proxies / curl)
  ?token=<token>                  (query — browsers can't set headers on
                                   new WebSocket())
  bad token → WS close 1008.  Daemon stores only the SHA-256 digest and
  compares with hmac.compare_digest.

identity at connect — per-user tickets (opt-in, --ws-app-credentials):
  an application that already authenticated a user in ITS OWN realm
  binds a short-lived single-use ticket to that user (ticket.bind, on a
  connection authenticated by an application credential), hands it to
  that user's client, and the client presents it in the SAME two places
  as the shared token above.  The daemon resolves it during the Upgrade
  and stamps '<app_id>:<user>' on the connection, so identity exists
  before the first frame instead of arriving as a message a client can
  simply not send.  An application credential binds and revokes; it
  cannot open a session.  With the flag absent, none of this exists and
  WS auth is the single shared token above.

per-application workspaces (the same file):
  {"<app_id>": {"credential": "...", "account": "<os account>",
               "workspace_root": "<dir owned by that account>"}}
  The application's users list, create and open workspaces under its
  root only; each workspace and everything the daemon writes into it
  (clone, staged files, .env, .gitconfig) belongs to the account, so
  --runner-uid-policy workspace-owner runs those sessions as it.  The
  daemon refuses to start if an account is missing, a root is not
  owned or reachable by its account, or two roots overlap.

preflight the WS daemon side (port + token file + auth mode):
  jaato-doctor --web-socket [host:]port

scaffold any transport:
  jaato-scaffold new client --transport in_process ...   # embedded
  jaato-scaffold new client --transport ipc ...          # local daemon (default)
  jaato-scaffold new client --transport ws ...           # remote daemon
The Python WS client needs the extra:  pip install 'jaato-sdk[ws]'
